questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Concrete & Steel Properties (IS 456 & IS 1786)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Hypothetical definitions and material behaviours.
  • Aim: Identify correct statements on characteristic strength, ten percent fines value, secant modulus, and carbon content effect.

Core Concepts:

  • Characteristic compressive strength \(f_{ck}\) (IS 456:2000, Cl. 6.2.4): Value below which ≤5% results fall → target mean \(= f_{ck} + 1.65\sigma\). If redefined as 50% (median), margin = 0 irrespective of quality control (\(\sigma\)).
  • Ten Percent Fines Value (TFV): Load (kN) causing 10% fines in aggregate (IS 2386 Part IV) → has units, is dimensional.
  • Secant modulus \(E_c = \sigma/\varepsilon\): Longer loading (1-day) includes creep → larger \(\varepsilon\) → smaller \(E_c\) compared to short-term (10-min) loading.
  • Carbon in steel: Increases pearlite fraction → higher yield / 0.2% proof stress (IS 1786).

Common pitfall: Confusing the 5% vs 50% definition of characteristic strength.

Solution:

  1. Option (A): If defined at 50% (median), target mean = characteristic strength → no margin regardless of QC (\(\sigma\)) → correct.
  2. Option (B): TFV has units (kN) → claim of being non-dimensional is incorrect → incorrect.
  3. Option (C): 1-day loading → creep strain ↑ → secant modulus ↓ vs 10-min loading → correct.
  4. Option (D): Carbon ↑ (0.2% → 0.8%) → 0.2% proof stress ↑ (mild to high tensile steel) → correct.

Final Answer:

Options A, C and D | Option(s): A; C; D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The figure shows a propped cantilever with uniform flexural rigidity EI (in N.m²) and subjected to a moment M (in N.m). Consider forces and displacements in the upward direction as positive.
Find the upward reaction at the propped support B (in N) when this support settles by (-Δ), given in metres.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Indeterminate Structures (Propped Cantilever)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Propped cantilever (fixed at A, roller at B), length \(L\), rigidity \(EI\). Clockwise moment \(M\) applied at B. Support B settles downward by \(\Delta\).
  • Aim: Upward reaction \(R_B\) at support B.

Core Concepts:

Method of Superposition (Compatibility): The net displacement at B must equal the prescribed settlement.

Standard Deflections (cantilever, measured at free end):

  • Due to end moment \(M\) (clockwise → downward): \(\delta_M = -\dfrac{ML^2}{2EI}\)
  • Due to upward point load \(R_B\) (upward): \(\delta_R = +\dfrac{R_B L^3}{3EI}\)

Solution:

  1. Sign convention: Upward force and upward displacement are positive. Settlement \(\Delta\) is downward, so the net displacement at B \(= -\Delta\).
  2. Apply compatibility condition:
    \[\delta_M + \delta_R = -\Delta\]\[-\dfrac{ML^2}{2EI} + \dfrac{R_B L^3}{3EI} = -\Delta\]
  3. Isolate \(R_B\):
    \[\dfrac{R_B L^3}{3EI} = \dfrac{ML^2}{2EI} - \Delta\]\[R_B = \dfrac{3EI}{L^3}\left(\dfrac{ML^2}{2EI} - \Delta\right) = \dfrac{3M}{2L} - \dfrac{3EI\Delta}{L^3}\]

Final Answer:

\(R_B = \dfrac{3M}{2L} - \dfrac{3EI\Delta}{L^3}\) | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Let the state of stress at a point in a body be the difference of two plane states of stress shown in the figure. Consider all the possible planes perpendicular to the x-y plane and passing through that point. The magnitude of the maximum compressive stress on any such plane is kσ₀, where k is equal to _______ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Complex Stresses & Mohr's Circle

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    State 1: Uniaxial tension, \(\sigma_{x1} = 3\sigma_0\), \(\sigma_{y1} = 0\), \(\tau_{xy1} = 0\).
    State 2: Uniaxial tension at \(45^\circ\), principal stresses \(\sigma_1 = 3\sigma_0\), \(\sigma_2 = 0\).
    Resultant State = State 1 \(-\) State 2.
  • Aim: Find the magnitude of the maximum compressive stress (\(k\sigma_0\)) of the resultant state.

Core Concepts:

  • Stress Transformation: \(\sigma_{x}' = \dfrac{\sigma_x+\sigma_y}{2} + \dfrac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{2}\cos(2\theta) + \tau_{xy}\sin(2\theta)\)
  • Principal Stresses: \(\sigma_{1,2} = \sigma_{avg} \pm R\), where \(R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{2}\right)^2 + \tau_{xy}^2}\)
  • Superposition: Stresses on the same coordinate planes are added or subtracted algebraically.

Solution:

  1. State 1 in x-y plane:
    \[\sigma_{x1} = 3\sigma_0,\quad \sigma_{y1} = 0,\quad \tau_{xy1} = 0\]
  2. Transform State 2 to x-y plane (\(\theta = 45^\circ\)):
    \[\sigma_{x2} = 3\sigma_0\cos^2(45^\circ) = 1.5\sigma_0\]\[\sigma_{y2} = 3\sigma_0\sin^2(45^\circ) = 1.5\sigma_0\]\[\tau_{xy2} = 3\sigma_0\sin(45^\circ)\cos(45^\circ) = 1.5\sigma_0\]
  3. Resultant (difference) state:
    \[\sigma_{x,net} = 3\sigma_0 - 1.5\sigma_0 = 1.5\sigma_0\]\[\sigma_{y,net} = 0 - 1.5\sigma_0 = -1.5\sigma_0\]\[\tau_{xy,net} = 0 - 1.5\sigma_0 = -1.5\sigma_0\]
  4. Mohr's Circle for resultant state:
    Average stress: \(\sigma_{avg} = \dfrac{1.5\sigma_0 + (-1.5\sigma_0)}{2} = 0\)
    Radius:
    \[R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1.5\sigma_0-(-1.5\sigma_0)}{2}\right)^2 + (-1.5\sigma_0)^2} = \sqrt{(1.5\sigma_0)^2+(1.5\sigma_0)^2} = \sqrt{4.5}\,\sigma_0 \approx 2.121\sigma_0\]
  5. Principal stresses: \(\sigma_p = 0 \pm 2.121\sigma_0\)
    Maximum compressive stress \(= -2.121\sigma_0\) → magnitude \(\approx \mathbf{2.1}\sigma_0\).

Final Answer:

2.1 (i.e., \(k = 2.1\)) | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: In the pin-jointed truss shown in the figure, the members that carry zero force are identified. Which of the following options is/are zero-force members?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Truss Analysis (Zero Force Members)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A pin-jointed truss with a vertical load of 60 kN at node B.
  • Aim: Identify all zero-force members from the given options (BC, EG, FI, JK).

Core Concepts:

  • Rule 1: If only two non-collinear members meet at a joint with no external load or reaction, both members are zero-force members.
  • Rule 2: If three members meet at a joint where two are collinear, the third (non-collinear) member is a zero-force member, provided no external load or reaction acts at that joint.

Solution:

  1. Joint A: Only two non-collinear members (AB and AC) meet here. No external load. → \(F_{AB} = 0\) and \(F_{AC} = 0\) (Rule 1).
  2. Joint C: Members AC, BC, and CE meet. Since AC and CE are collinear and \(F_{AC} = 0\), vertical equilibrium requires → \(F_{BC} = 0\) (Rule 2).
  3. Joint H: Two non-collinear members (FH and HI) meet. No external load. → \(F_{FH} = 0\) and \(F_{HI} = 0\) (Rule 1).
  4. Joint K: Members JK, IK, and MK meet. IK and MK are collinear. No external horizontal load at K. → \(F_{JK} = 0\) (Rule 2).
  5. Verification with official key confirms BC and JK are zero-force members.

Final Answer:

BC and JK | Option(s): A and D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A steel beam supported by three parallel pin-jointed steel rods is shown in the figure. The moment of inertia of the beam is 8 × 10⁷ mm⁴. Take modulus of elasticity of steel as 210 GPa. The beam is subjected to uniformly distributed load of 6.25 kN/m, including its self-weight.
The axial force (in kN) in the centre rod CD is _______ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Deflection & Compatibility — Beam-Rod System

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Steel beam supported by three parallel pin-jointed steel rods (A, C, E); \(I = 8 \times 10^7~mm^4\), \(E = 210~GPa\), UDL \(w = 6.25~kN/m\), outer rod diameter = 12 mm, centre rod diameter = 30 mm, rod spacing = 2 m (symmetric), rod length = 1 m.
  • Aim: Find the axial force in the centre rod C in kN.

Core Concepts:

  • Equilibrium: \(2T_A + T_C = wL_{beam}\)
  • Compatibility: \(\Delta_{rod,C} = \Delta_{rod,A} + \Delta_{bending,centre}\)
  • Axial deformation: \(\Delta_{rod} = \dfrac{TL}{AE}\)
  • Beam deflection (superposition): \(\Delta_{bending} = \dfrac{5wL_{beam}^4}{384EI} - \dfrac{T_C L_{beam}^3}{48EI}\)

Solution:

  1. Unit conversions: \(E = 210{,}000~N/mm^2\), \(w = 6.25~N/mm\), \(L_{beam} = 4000~mm\), \(L_{rod} = 1000~mm\)
    \(A_{out} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(12)^2 = 113.097~mm^2\), \(A_{in} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(30)^2 = 706.858~mm^2\)
  2. Equilibrium: Total load \(= 6.25 \times 4000 = 25{,}000~N\)
    \[T_A = \dfrac{25{,}000 - T_C}{2}\]
  3. Compatibility equation (substituting \(T_A\)):
    \[\dfrac{T_C L_{rod}}{A_{in} E} + \dfrac{T_C L_{rod}}{2A_{out} E} + \dfrac{T_C L_{beam}^3}{48EI} = \dfrac{25{,}000 \cdot L_{rod}}{2A_{out} E} + \dfrac{5wL_{beam}^4}{384EI}\]
  4. Compute LHS coefficients (mm/N):
    Term 1: \(\dfrac{1000}{706.858 \times 210{,}000} = 6.737 \times 10^{-6}\)
    Term 2: \(\dfrac{1000}{2 \times 113.097 \times 210{,}000} = 21.052 \times 10^{-6}\)
    Term 3: \(\dfrac{4000^3}{48 \times 210{,}000 \times 8 \times 10^7} = 79.365 \times 10^{-6}\)
    Total LHS coefficient \(= 107.154 \times 10^{-6}~mm/N\)
  5. Compute RHS (mm):
    Term 1: \(25{,}000 \times 21.052 \times 10^{-6} = 0.5263~mm\)
    Term 2: \(\dfrac{5 \times 6.25 \times 4000^4}{384 \times 210{,}000 \times 8 \times 10^7} = 1.2401~mm\)
    Total RHS \(= 1.7664~mm\)
  6. Solve for \(T_C\):
    \[T_C = \dfrac{1.7664}{107.154 \times 10^{-6}} = 16{,}484.6~N \approx \mathbf{16.5}~kN\]

Final Answer:

16.5 kN | Option(s): Range 16.3 to 16.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The three-dimensional state of stress at a point is given by

\[\sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 40 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \text{MPa.} \]

The maximum shear stress at the point is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Theory of Elasticity / Maximum Shear Stress

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Stress tensor (in principal form):\[\sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 40 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \text{ MPa}\]
  • Aim: Find the maximum shear stress.

Core Concepts:

Since the tensor is already in principal form, the principal stresses are read directly from the diagonal: \(\sigma_1 = 40\) MPa, \(\sigma_2 = 10\) MPa, \(\sigma_3 = 0\) MPa.

Maximum shear stress (absolute):\[\tau_{\max} = \dfrac{\sigma_{\max} - \sigma_{\min}}{2}\]This corresponds to the radius of the largest Mohr's circle.

Common Pitfall: Taking the difference of only two adjacent principal stresses instead of the absolute maximum and minimum.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Principal stresses: \(\sigma_{\max} = 40\) MPa, \(\sigma_{\min} = 0\) MPa
  2. \[\tau_{\max} = \dfrac{40 - 0}{2} = 20 \text{ MPa}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\tau_{\max} = 20\) MPa | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The elements that DO NOT increase the strength of structural steel are
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Material Properties / Effects of Alloying Elements

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Elements: Carbon, Manganese, Sulphur, Chlorine.
  • Aim: Identify elements that do not increase the strength of structural steel.

Core Concepts:

  • Carbon: Increases hardness and tensile strength via interstitial solid solution strengthening.
  • Manganese: Provides solid solution strengthening and improves hardenability.
  • Sulphur: An impurity that forms brittle MnS/FeS inclusions, promotes hot shortness, and reduces transverse strength and impact resistance.
  • Chlorine: Not a standard alloying element; causes chloride-induced corrosion, weakening the structure over time.
  • Reference: IS 2062 specifies limits of Sulphur ≤ 0.045% for weldable structural steel; Chlorine is not an intentional alloying element.

Common Pitfall: Confusing strength with ductility (e.g., Carbon increases strength but can decrease ductility); assuming all elements listed are beneficial alloying additions.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. (A) Carbon: Increases tensile strength → increases strength
  2. (B) Manganese: Solid solution strengthening → increases strength
  3. (C) Sulphur: Forms brittle inclusions, reduces toughness and strength → does NOT increase strength ✓
  4. (D) Chlorine: Causes corrosion and structural weakening → does NOT increase strength ✓

Final Answer:

Final Answer: C (Sulphur) and D (Chlorine) do not increase strength | Option(s): C, D

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The plane frame shown in the figure has fixed support at joint A, hinge support at joint F, and roller support at joint I. In the figure, A to I indicate joints of the frame.




If the axial deformations are neglected, the degree of kinematic indeterminacy is _________ (in integer).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Indeterminacy / Kinematic Indeterminacy

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Plane frame with 9 joints (A to I)
    • Fixed support at A (3 restraints), hinge support at F (2 restraints), roller support at I (1 restraint)
    • 12 members; axial deformations neglected
  • Aim: Determine the degree of kinematic indeterminacy (\(D_k\)).

Core Concepts:

Kinematic Indeterminacy (\(D_k\)): The number of independent displacement components needed to define the deformed shape.

  • With axial deformations: \(D_k = 3j - r\)
  • Axial deformations neglected: \(D_k = 3j - r - m\) (each inextensible member adds one constraint)

Restraints: Fixed = 3 (\(u_x, u_y, \theta_z = 0\)); Hinge/Pin = 2 (\(u_x, u_y = 0\)); Roller = 1 (\(u_y = 0\)).

Common Pitfall: Forgetting internal constraints from axial neglect; mis-counting members or restraints.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Count joints: \(j = 9\) (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I)

  2. Count members:
    Verticals: A-B, B-C, F-E, E-D, I-H, H-G = 6
    Horizontals: A-F, F-I, B-E, E-H, C-D, D-G = 6
    Total: \(m = 12\)

  3. Count external restraints:
    Fixed at A = 3; Hinge at F = 2; Roller at I = 1
    Total: \(r = 6\)

  4. Apply formula (axial deformations neglected):\[D_k = 3j - r - m = 3(9) - 6 - 12 = 27 - 6 - 12 = 9\]

Sanity check: \(D_k = 9\) is physically consistent for a multi-story frame — e.g., 6 joint rotations + 3 independent sway modes.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 9

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Find the correct match between the plane stress states and the Mohr’s circles.
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Complex Stresses / Mohr's Circle

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Analysis
  • Given Data: Four visual representations of 2D plane stress states (P, Q, R, S) and four Mohr's circles (I, II, III, IV).
  • Aim: Match the correct plane stress state to its corresponding Mohr's circle representation.

Core Concepts:

Mohr's Circle is a graphical representation used to find normal and shear stresses on inclined planes.

  • Center Coordinate: \((C, 0)\) where \(C = \dfrac{\sigma_x + \sigma_y}{2}\)
  • Radius: \(R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\right)^2 + \tau_{xy}^2}\)
  • Sign Convention: Tensile normal stress (\(\sigma\)) is positive (plotted to the right); compressive is negative (plotted to the left).

Solution Method:

Evaluate the center and radius for each given stress block diagram and find the matching visual circle.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. State (P): Uniaxial Tension
    \(\sigma_x = 10\), \(\sigma_y = 0\), \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)
    Center: \(C = \dfrac{10 + 0}{2} = 5\)
    Radius: \(R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{10-0}{2}\right)^2 + 0} = 5\)
    The circle touches the origin and lies entirely on the positive \(\sigma\) axis. → Matches Circle (III).

  2. State (Q): Pure Shear
    \(\sigma_x = 0\), \(\sigma_y = 0\), \(\tau_{xy} = \pm10\)
    Center: \(C = \dfrac{0+0}{2} = 0\)
    Radius: \(R = \sqrt{0 + 10^2} = 10\)
    The circle is perfectly centered at the origin. → Matches Circle (IV).

  3. State (R): Uniaxial Compression
    \(\sigma_x = 0\), \(\sigma_y = -10\), \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)
    Center: \(C = \dfrac{0 - 10}{2} = -5\)
    Radius: \(R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{0-(-10)}{2}\right)^2 + 0} = 5\)
    The circle touches the origin and lies entirely on the negative \(\sigma\) axis. → Matches Circle (I).

  4. State (S): Biaxial (Hydrostatic) Compression
    \(\sigma_x = -10\), \(\sigma_y = -10\), \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)
    Center: \(C = \dfrac{-10-10}{2} = -10\)
    Radius: \(R = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{-10-(-10)}{2}\right)^2 + 0} = 0\)
    The circle degenerates into a single point at \(-10\) on the \(\sigma\) axis. → Matches Circle (II).

Final Answer:

Final Answer: (P)-(III); (Q)-(IV); (R)-(I); (S)-(II) | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The beam shown in the figure is subjected to a uniformly distributed downward load of intensity \( q \) between supports A and B.




Considering the upward reactions as positive, the support reactions are
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Statically Determinate Beams / Internal Hinges

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Continuous beam with a pin support at A, and roller supports at B and C.
    • An internal hinge is located between A and B.
    • Span lengths: A to hinge \(= l\); hinge to B \(= l\); B to C \(= l\). Total length \(= 3l\).
    • Loading: A uniformly distributed load (UDL) of intensity \(q\) acts downwards continuously from support A to support B.
    • Sign convention: Upward reactions are positive.
  • Aim: Determine the correct magnitude and direction of the support reactions \(R_A\), \(R_B\), and \(R_C\).

Core Concepts:

Static Equilibrium: For a rigid body in equilibrium, the sum of all forces and the sum of all moments about any point must be zero (\(\sum F_y = 0\), \(\sum M = 0\)).

Internal Hinge Property: An internal hinge cannot resist or transfer bending moments. Therefore, the bending moment exactly at the hinge is always zero (\(M_H = 0\)). This provides an additional equilibrium equation, allowing us to solve systems that might otherwise appear statically indeterminate.

Free Body Diagrams (FBD): The most reliable method for beams with internal hinges is to structurally "break" the beam at the hinge and draw separate FBDs for the resulting segments. The hinge transfers only shear force (vertical and horizontal), but no moment.

Solution Method:

  1. Separate the beam at the internal hinge (\(H\)) into a left segment (\(AH\)) and a right segment (\(HBC\)).
  2. Solve the left segment first to find the reaction at A (\(R_A\)) and the internal shear force transferred at the hinge (\(V_H\)).
  3. Apply this calculated hinge shear force to the right segment (in the opposite direction, per Newton's Third Law) and use moment equilibrium to find \(R_C\) and \(R_B\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Analyze the Left Segment (\(A\) to \(H\))

  • This segment has length \(l\). It is supported by a pin at \(A\) and the hinge at \(H\).
  • It carries a downward UDL of \(q\) over its entire length \(l\). The total load is \(ql\), acting at the centroid (\(l/2\) from \(A\)).
  • Taking moments about the hinge \(H\) (\(\sum M_H = 0\)):\[R_A \cdot l - (q \cdot l) \cdot \left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right) = 0\]\[R_A \cdot l = \dfrac{ql^2}{2}\]\[R_A = \dfrac{ql}{2} \text{ (acting upwards)}\]
  • Sum of vertical forces (\(\sum F_y = 0\)):\[R_A - ql + V_H = 0\]\[\dfrac{ql}{2} - ql + V_H = 0 \implies V_H = \dfrac{ql}{2} \text{ (acting upwards on segment AH)}\]
  • Crucial Transfer Step: Because the hinge supports segment \(AH\) with an upward force of \(\dfrac{ql}{2}\), segment \(AH\) pushes downwards on segment \(HBC\) with a force of \(P_H = \dfrac{ql}{2}\).

Step 2: Analyze the Right Segment (\(H\) to \(C\))

  • This segment has length \(2l\) (from \(H\) to \(B\) is \(l\), from \(B\) to \(C\) is \(l\)).
  • It carries the transferred point load \(P_H = \dfrac{ql}{2}\) downwards at \(H\).
  • It carries a UDL of \(q\) downwards between \(H\) and \(B\) (length \(l\)). The total UDL load on this segment is \(ql\), acting at \(l/2\) from \(B\).
  • Taking moments about support \(B\) (\(\sum M_B = 0\)), counter-clockwise positive:\[(P_H \cdot l) + \left(q \cdot l \cdot \dfrac{l}{2}\right) + (R_C \cdot l) = 0\]\[\left(\dfrac{ql}{2} \cdot l\right) + \dfrac{ql^2}{2} + R_C \cdot l = 0\]\[\dfrac{ql^2}{2} + \dfrac{ql^2}{2} + R_C \cdot l = 0\]\[ql^2 + R_C \cdot l = 0 \implies R_C = -ql \text{ (acting downwards)}\]
  • Sum of vertical forces (\(\sum F_y = 0\)):\[R_B + R_C - P_H - (q \cdot l) = 0\]\[R_B + (-ql) - \dfrac{ql}{2} - ql = 0\]\[R_B = 2ql + \dfrac{ql}{2} = \dfrac{5ql}{2} \text{ (acting upwards)}\]

Step 3: Global Sanity Check

  • \(\sum F_{\text{upward}} = R_A + R_B + R_C = \dfrac{ql}{2} + \dfrac{5ql}{2} - ql = 3ql - ql = 2ql\)
  • \(\sum F_{\text{downward}} = \text{UDL over } 2l = q \cdot 2l = 2ql\) ✓
  • The system is in perfect equilibrium.

Final Answer:

\(R_A = \dfrac{ql}{2}\);   \(R_B = \dfrac{5ql}{2}\);   \(R_C = -ql\)  | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A homogeneous shaft PQR with fixed supports at both ends is subjected to a torsional moment T at point Q, as shown in the figure. The polar moments of inertia of the portions PQ and QR of the shaft with circular cross-sections are \( J_1 \) and \( J_2 \), respectively. The torsional moment reactions at the supports P and R are \( T_P \) and \( T_R \), respectively.




If \( T_P/T_R = 4 \) and \( J_1/J_2 = 2 \), the ratio of the lengths \( L_1/L_2 \) is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Torsion of Shafts

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Support conditions: Fixed at both ends (P and R).
    • Torque applied: \(T\) at point Q.
    • Reaction ratio: \(T_P / T_R = 4\)
    • Polar moment of inertia ratio: \(J_1 / J_2 = 2\)
  • Aim: Find the length ratio \(L_1 / L_2\).

Core Concepts:

Kinematic Compatibility: For a shaft fixed at both ends, the total angle of twist from one end to the other is zero. Therefore, the absolute angle of twist at the loading point Q must be the same whether calculated from end P or end R.

Torsion Formula: The angle of twist \(\theta\) is given by \[\theta = \dfrac{T L}{G J}\] where \(T\) is the internal torque, \(L\) is the length, \(G\) is the shear modulus (constant for a homogeneous material), and \(J\) is the polar moment of inertia.

Solution Method:

  1. Establish the compatibility equation equating the twist at Q from both fixed ends.
  2. Substitute the given ratios into the compatibility equation.
  3. Solve algebraically for the length ratio.

Common Pitfall: Forgetting that internal torques in sections PQ and QR are equal to the support reactions \(T_P\) and \(T_R\) respectively, due to static equilibrium.

Step-by-Step Execution:

Compatibility Equation:

\[\theta_{Q/P} = \theta_{Q/R}\]\[\dfrac{T_P L_1}{G J_1} = \dfrac{T_R L_2}{G J_2}\]

Rearranging for the target ratio:

\[\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = \left(\dfrac{T_R}{T_P}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{J_1}{J_2}\right)\]

Substituting given values: \(T_P/T_R = 4\), so \(T_R/T_P = 1/4 = 0.25\); and \(J_1/J_2 = 2\):

\[\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = (0.25) \times 2 = 0.50\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.50 | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The plane truss shown in the figure has 13 joints and 22 members. The truss is made of a homogeneous, prismatic, linearly elastic material. All members have identical axial rigidity. A to M indicate the joints of the truss. The truss has pin supports at joints A and L and roller support at joint K. The truss is subjected to a 10 kN vertically downward force at joint H and a 10 kN horizontal force in the rightward direction at joint B as shown.




The magnitude of the reaction (in kN) at the pin support L is _____________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Complex Truss Systems

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • 13 joints, 22 members
    • Supports: Pin at A, Pin at L, Roller at K
    • Loading: 10 kN downward at H, 10 kN rightward at B
  • Aim: Find the magnitude of the reaction at pin support L.

Core Concepts:

  • Global Equilibrium: \(\sum F_x = 0\), \(\sum F_y = 0\), \(\sum M = 0\)
  • Sub-structuring / Internal Hinges: When a truss is composed of rigid sub-blocks connected by a single node, that connecting node acts as an internal hinge transferring only axial forces (zero internal moment).

Solution Method:

The structure has 5 support reaction components (\(A_x, A_y, L_x, L_y, K_x\)), making it externally statically indeterminate to the 2nd degree. However, the structure can be split into three rigid blocks connected only at single nodes D and J. Taking moments about these "hinge" nodes for isolated blocks provides the extra equations needed.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Right Block (Nodes J, K, L, M):
    Connected to the rest of the truss solely at J(6,2). Taking moments about J (\(\sum M_J^{\text{right}} = 0\)):
    — Moment of \(L_y\): lever arm = 0 (L is directly below J)
    — Moment of \(K_x\): lever arm = 0 (K is on the same horizontal line as J)
    — Moment of \(L_x\): acts at \(y=0\), lever arm = 2m about J(\(y=2\))\[L_x \times 2 = 0 \implies L_x = 0 \text{ kN}\]

  2. Analyze Left Block (Nodes A, B, C, D):
    Connected to the middle block solely at D(2,2). Taking moments about D (\(\sum M_D^{\text{left}} = 0\)):
    The 10 kN horizontal force at B passes through the horizontal line of D → moment = 0.\[2A_x - 2A_y = 0 \implies A_x = A_y\]

  3. Global Equilibrium — Moments about A(0,0):\[-(10 \times 2) - (10 \times 5) + L_y \times 6 + K_x \times 2 = 0\]\[3L_y + K_x = 35 \quad \text{--- (Eq. I)}\]

  4. Global Equilibrium — Sum of forces in Y:\[A_y - 10 + L_y = 0 \implies A_y + L_y = 10 \quad \text{--- (Eq. II)}\]

  5. Global Equilibrium — Sum of forces in X:
    Since \(L_x = 0\) and \(A_x = A_y\):\[A_y + 10 - K_x = 0 \implies K_x = A_y + 10 \quad \text{--- (Eq. III)}\]

  6. Solve the System:
    Substitute (Eq. III) into (Eq. I):\[3L_y + A_y + 10 = 35 \implies 3L_y + A_y = 25 \quad \text{--- (Eq. IV)}\]
    From (Eq. II): \(A_y = 10 - L_y\). Substitute into (Eq. IV):\[3L_y + (10 - L_y) = 25 \implies 2L_y = 15 \implies L_y = 7.5 \text{ kN}\]

  7. Calculate Final Magnitude at L:\[|\vec{R}_L| = \sqrt{L_x^2 + L_y^2} = \sqrt{0^2 + 7.5^2} = 7.5 \text{ kN}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.5 kN | Option(s): NAT

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A 3 m long, horizontal, rigid, uniform beam PQ has negligible mass. The beam is subjected to a 3 kN concentrated vertically downward force at 1 m from P, as shown in the figure. The beam is resting on vertical linear springs at the ends P and Q. For the spring at the end P, the spring constant \( K_P = 100 \) kN/m.



If the beam DOES NOT rotate under the application of the force and displaces only vertically, the value of the spring constant \( K_Q \) (in kN/m) for the spring at the end Q is
questions.explanation:
Strength of Materials | Rigid Beams on Elastic Supports (Spring Stiffness)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Beam length \(L = 3\text{ m}\); concentrated vertical load \(P = 3\text{ kN}\) at 1 m from P; spring stiffness at P, \(K_P = 100\text{ kN/m}\); beam rigid, uniform, negligible mass; pure vertical translation (no rotation).
  • Aim: Find the value of spring constant \(K_Q\) (kN/m) at Q.

Core Concepts:

  • Compatibility: For a rigid beam with zero rotation, vertical deflection at P equals deflection at Q (\(\delta_P = \delta_Q = \delta\)).
  • Hooke's Law: Spring reaction \(F = K \times \delta\).
  • Static equilibrium: \(\sum F_y = 0\) and \(\sum M = 0\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Let uniform downward deflection of rigid beam \(= \delta\) (m).
    Reaction at P: \(F_P = 100\delta\) kN (upward).
    Reaction at Q: \(F_Q = K_Q \delta\) kN (upward).
  2. Moment equilibrium about P:
    \[3 \times 1 = F_Q \times 3 \implies F_Q = 1\text{ kN} \]
  3. Vertical force equilibrium:
    \[F_P = 3 - 1 = 2\text{ kN} \]
  4. Find \(\delta\) from spring at P:
    \[\delta = \dfrac{F_P}{K_P} = \dfrac{2}{100} = 0.02\text{ m} \]
  5. Find \(K_Q\):
    \[K_Q = \dfrac{F_Q}{\delta} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} = 50\text{ kN/m} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50 kN/m | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
For a thin-walled section shown in the figure, points P, Q, and R are located on the major bending axis X – X of the section. Point Q is located on the web whereas point S is located at the intersection of the web and the top flange of the section.



Qualitatively, the shear center of the section lies at
questions.explanation:
Strength of Materials | Thin-Walled Open Sections | Shear Centre

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Thin-walled section with top/bottom flanges having 6 cm projection on left of web and 3 cm on right; major bending axis X–X; points P (left), Q (on web), R (right) on X–X; S at top flange–web intersection.
  • Aim: Qualitative location of the shear centre.

Core Concepts:

Shear centre is the unique point where an applied transverse shear force produces pure bending with zero torsion (net torque from shear flows = 0). For open thin-walled sections, horizontal shear flow in flanges is proportional to distance from the free end — unequal flange projections create an unbalanced torsional couple.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Flanges are asymmetric: left overhang = 6 cm, right overhang = 3 cm.
  2. Under vertical shear, shear flow in flanges is proportional to flange length from free end.
  3. Longer left flange (6 cm) produces a larger horizontal shear force and larger moment arm than the shorter right flange (3 cm).
  4. Net torsional couple is clockwise; to nullify this torque, the line of action of total vertical shear must shift to the right of the web (towards the shorter flange side).
  5. Among the given options, this shift places the shear centre at point R on the major axis X–X.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: R | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A linearly elastic beam of length \( 2l \) with flexural rigidity \( EI \) has negligible mass. A massless spring with a spring constant \( k \) and a rigid block of mass \( m \) are attached to the beam as shown in the figure.



The natural frequency of this system is
questions.explanation:
Structural Dynamics | Natural Frequency

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Beam length \(= 2l\)
    Flexural rigidity \(= EI\)
    Spring constant \(= k\)
    Rigid block mass \(= m\)
    The visual layout implies the spring and the beam's midspan undergo the same vertical deflection when the mass \(m\) oscillates.
  • Aim: Find the natural frequency of the system.

Core Concepts:

Equivalent Stiffness (\(k_{eq}\)): For a single degree of freedom (SDOF) undamped system, natural frequency \(\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_{eq}}{m}}\).

Beam Stiffness (\(k_b\)): The stiffness of a simply supported beam subject to a central point load is derived from its deflection formula: \(\Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{48EI}\). Thus, \(k_b = \dfrac{P}{\Delta} = \dfrac{48EI}{L^3}\).

Spring Configuration: Since the spring and beam are connected such that they deform by the same amount under the dynamic action of the mass, they act in parallel. For parallel springs, \(k_{eq} = k_1 + k_2\).

Solution Method:

  • Substitute the given length \(L = 2l\) into the beam stiffness formula.
  • Add the beam's equivalent stiffness to the spring constant \(k\).
  • Plug the combined stiffness into the natural frequency equation.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine beam stiffness \(k_b\): Total length \(L = 2l\).
    \[k_b = \dfrac{48EI}{(2l)^3} = \dfrac{48EI}{8l^3} = \dfrac{6EI}{l^3} \]
  2. Determine equivalent stiffness \(k_{eq}\): Since they are in parallel,
    \[k_{eq} = k + k_b = k + \dfrac{6EI}{l^3} = \dfrac{kl^3 + 6EI}{l^3} \]
  3. Calculate natural frequency \(\omega_n\):
    \[\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_{eq}}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{kl^3 + 6EI}{l^3}}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{kl^3 + 6EI}{ml^3}} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{kl^3 + 6EI}{ml^3}}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A homogeneous, prismatic, linearly elastic steel bar fixed at both the ends has a slenderness ratio (\( l/r \)) of 105, where \( l \) is the bar length and \( r \) is the radius of gyration. The coefficient of thermal expansion of steel is \( 12 \times 10^{-6} /°C \). Consider the effective length of the steel bar as \( 0.5l \) and neglect the self-weight of the bar.

The differential increase in temperature (rounded off to the nearest integer) at which the bar buckles is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Thermal Stresses & Column Buckling

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Fixed-fixed steel bar
    Slenderness ratio \(\dfrac{l}{r} = 105\)
    Thermal expansion coefficient \(\alpha = 12 \times 10^{-6} \text{ /}^\circ\text{C}\)
    Effective length \(L_{eff} = 0.5l\)
  • Aim: Find the differential temperature \(\Delta T\) at which the bar buckles.

Core Concepts:

Thermal Stress: A bar prevented from expanding will develop a compressive thermal stress:
\[\sigma_{th} = E \alpha \Delta T \]

Euler's Buckling Stress: The critical compressive stress at which a slender column buckles is:
\[\sigma_{cr} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E}{\lambda_{eff}^2} \]
where \(\lambda_{eff} = \dfrac{L_{eff}}{r}\).

Buckling Condition: Buckling occurs when the induced thermal stress equals the critical buckling stress (\(\sigma_{th} = \sigma_{cr}\)). Note that Young's Modulus (\(E\)) mathematically cancels out.

Solution Method:

  • Calculate the effective slenderness ratio \(\lambda_{eff}\).
  • Equate \(\sigma_{th}\) and \(\sigma_{cr}\) and solve for \(\Delta T\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate effective slenderness ratio: Given \(\dfrac{l}{r} = 105\) and \(L_{eff} = 0.5l\).
    \[\lambda_{eff} = \dfrac{L_{eff}}{r} = 0.5 \times \dfrac{l}{r} = 0.5 \times 105 = 52.5 \]
  2. Equate thermal and buckling stresses:
    \[E \alpha \Delta T = \dfrac{\pi^2 E}{\lambda_{eff}^2} \]\[\alpha \Delta T = \dfrac{\pi^2}{52.5^2} \]
  3. Solve for \(\Delta T\):
    \[12 \times 10^{-6} \times \Delta T = \dfrac{\pi^2}{2756.25} \]\[12 \times 10^{-6} \times \Delta T = 0.0035805 \]\[\Delta T = \dfrac{0.0035805}{12 \times 10^{-6}} = 298.375 ^\circ\text{C} \]
    Round to the nearest integer: \(\Delta T \approx 298 ^\circ\text{C}\)

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(298 ^\circ\text{C}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
For the 6 m long horizontal cantilever beam PQR shown in the figure, Q is the midpoint. Segment PQ of the beam has flexural rigidity EI = \( 2 \times 10^5 \) kN.m² whereas the segment QR has infinite flexural rigidity. Segment QR is subjected to uniformly distributed, vertically downward load of 5 kN/m.



The magnitude of the vertical displacement (in mm) at point Q is _________ (rounded off to 3 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Beams

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Total beam length PQR = 6 m.
    Segment PQ length = 3 m, flexural rigidity \(EI = 2 \times 10^5\text{ kN.m}^2\).
    Segment QR length = 3 m, infinite flexural rigidity (\(EI = \infty\)).
    Load on QR = 5 kN/m UDL acting vertically downward.
  • Aim: Determine the vertical displacement at point Q in mm, rounded to 3 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Rigid Body Mechanics: Segment QR has infinite flexural rigidity — it will not bend or deform, acting as a rigid lever arm transferring applied loads directly to point Q.

Equivalent Nodal Loads: A load on a rigid attachment can be statically transferred to the elastic support point (Q) as an equivalent point load and a concentrated bending moment.

Superposition Theorem: Total deflection at Q = sum of individual deflections caused by the equivalent point load and moment acting independently on cantilever PQ.

Standard Cantilever Deflection Formulas (Euler-Bernoulli Beam Theory):

  • Deflection due to point load \(W\) at free end: \(\delta_W = \dfrac{WL^3}{3EI}\)
  • Deflection due to concentrated moment \(M\) at free end: \(\delta_M = \dfrac{ML^2}{2EI}\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Rigid Segment QR:
    UDL \(= 5\text{ kN/m}\) over length 3 m.
    Total downward force: \(W = 5 \times 3 = 15\text{ kN}\).
    Resultant acts at centroid of UDL, i.e., \(1.5\text{ m}\) from Q.
  2. Transfer Load to Point Q:
    Vertical point load: \(V_Q = 15\text{ kN}\) (downward).
    Moment at Q: \(M_Q = 15 \times 1.5 = 22.5\text{ kN.m}\) (clockwise, causing downward deflection).
  3. Calculate Deflections for Segment PQ (Length \(L = 3\text{ m}\)):
    Deflection due to point load \(V_Q\):
    \[\delta_1 = \dfrac{V_Q L^3}{3EI} = \dfrac{15 \times 27}{3EI} = \dfrac{135}{EI} \]
    Deflection due to moment \(M_Q\):
    \[\delta_2 = \dfrac{M_Q L^2}{2EI} = \dfrac{22.5 \times 9}{2EI} = \dfrac{101.25}{EI} \]
  4. Total Deflection at Q:
    Both loads cause downward displacement, so they add up:
    \[\delta_Q = \delta_1 + \delta_2 = \dfrac{135}{EI} + \dfrac{101.25}{EI} = \dfrac{236.25}{EI} \]
  5. Substitute Values and Convert Units:
    Given \(EI = 2 \times 10^5\text{ kN.m}^2\):
    \[\delta_Q = \dfrac{236.25}{200000} = 0.00118125\text{ m} \]
    Convert to mm (multiply by 1000):
    \[\delta_Q = 1.18125\text{ mm} \approx 1.181\text{ mm} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.181 mm | Accepted key range: [1.176 to 1.186]

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The horizontal beam PQRS shown in the figure has a fixed support at point P, an internal hinge at point Q, and a pin support at point R. A concentrated vertically downward load (V) of 10 kN can act at any point over the entire length of the beam.



The maximum magnitude of the moment reaction (in kN.m) that can act at the support P due to V is _________ (in integer).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Influence Lines & Reactions

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Beam PQRS with total length 30 m (PQ = 15 m, QR = 10 m, RS = 5 m).
    Supports: Fixed at P, internal hinge at Q, pin/roller support at R.
    Load: Moving vertically downward concentrated load \(V = 10\text{ kN}\).
  • Aim: Find the maximum magnitude of the moment reaction at fixed support P (\(M_P\)) in kN.m.

Core Concepts:

Beam Kinematics & Support Reactions: An internal hinge (like Q) cannot transfer bending moment — it can only transfer shear force (vertical reaction). The structure is therefore split into two parts:

  • Cantilever PQ: Fixed at P, provides support to segment QRS at hinge Q.
  • Overhanging Beam QRS: Simply supported by the hinge at Q and the pin at R.

Influence Line Diagrams (ILD): The concept of finding the critical position of a moving load that maximizes a specific reaction or internal force. For a cantilever, the fixed end moment is the applied force multiplied by its perpendicular distance to the fixed support.

Solution Method:

  • Isolate segment QRS and analyze it as a simply supported beam with an overhang.
  • Determine the vertical reaction transferred to hinge Q (\(R_Q\)) for different load positions.
  • Recognize that cantilever PQ only feels the load transferred through hinge Q, or load acting directly on PQ.
  • Calculate \(M_P\) by placing the 10 kN load at critical points (P, Q, R, S) to find the absolute maximum magnitude.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Structural Interaction: Any downward force applied to QRS transfers a fractional downward load to Q. By Newton's Third Law, this acts as a downward point load on the tip of cantilever PQ.
  2. Critical Position 1 — Load at Q:
    The entire 10 kN is directly supported by cantilever PQ at its free end.
    \[M_P = F_Q \times \text{(Distance PQ)} = 10 \times 15 = 150\text{ kN.m (Hogging)} \]
  3. Critical Position 2 — Load between P and Q:
    Let load act at distance \(x\) from P: \(M_P = 10 \times x\). Maximum occurs at \(x = 15\text{ m}\) (at Q), again yielding 150 kN.m.
  4. Critical Position 3 — Load at free end S:
    Analyze FBD of segment QRS. Taking moments about pin support R (\(\sum M_R = 0\)):
    \[R_Q \times 10 - 10 \times 5 = 0 \implies R_Q = 5\text{ kN (upward at Q)} \]
    By Newton's 3rd Law, hinge Q pulls upward on cantilever PQ with 5 kN.
    \[M_P = 5 \times 15 = 75\text{ kN.m (Sagging)} \]
  5. Compare Magnitudes:
    • Load at Q: \(|-150| = 150\text{ kN.m}\)
    • Load at S: \(|+75| = 75\text{ kN.m}\)
    The maximum magnitude is 150 kN.m.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 150 kN.m | Accepted key range: [150 to 150]

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A hanger is made of two bars of different sizes. Each bar has a square cross-section. The hanger is loaded by three-point loads in the mid vertical plane as shown in the figure. Ignore the self-weight of the hanger. What is the maximum tensile stress in N/mm² anywhere in the hanger without considering stress concentration effects?
questions.explanation:
Strength of Materials | Simple Axial Stress

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Upper bar: square cross-section, side \(= 100\) mm
    • Lower bar: square cross-section, side \(= 50\) mm
    • Three downward point loads: \(100\) kN, \(100\) kN, \(50\) kN (upper bar supports all three)
    • Self-weight ignored
  • Aim: Maximum tensile stress (N/mm²) anywhere in the hanger (no stress concentration).

Core Concepts:

Axial tensile stress: \(\sigma = \dfrac{P}{A}\) (uniform across square section).

Force diagram: Upper bar carries the total load below the fixed support (sum of all three loads \(= 250\) kN); lower bar carries only the bottom load (\(50\) kN).

Unit conversion: \(1\text{ kN} = 10^3\text{ N}\); stress in N/mm² (MPa).

Solution Method:

Compute cross-sectional areas → identify axial force in each segment from statics → \(\sigma = P \times 10^3 / A\) → select the larger value.

Common pitfall: Assuming the lower bar carries more load (incorrect force path).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Areas:
    Upper: \(A_u = 100 \times 100 = 10{,}000 \text{ mm}^2\)
    Lower: \(A_l = 50 \times 50 = 2{,}500 \text{ mm}^2\)
  2. Axial Forces:
    \(P_{\text{upper}} = 100 + 100 + 50 = 250 \text{ kN} = 250 \times 10^3 \text{ N}\)
    \(P_{\text{lower}} = 50 \text{ kN} = 50 \times 10^3 \text{ N}\)
  3. Stresses:\[\sigma_{\text{upper}} = \dfrac{250 \times 10^3}{10{,}000} = 25 \text{ N/mm}^2 \]\[\sigma_{\text{lower}} = \dfrac{50 \times 10^3}{2{,}500} = 20 \text{ N/mm}^2 \]
  4. Maximum tensile stress \(= 25 \text{ N/mm}^2\) (occurs in the upper bar).
SectionForce (N)Area (mm²)Stress (N/mm²)
Upper250,00010,00025
Lower50,0002,50020

Final Answer:

25.0 N/mm² | Correct Option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Consider the following three structures:
Structure I: Beam with hinge support at A, roller at C, guided roller at E, and internal hinges at B and D
Structure II: Pin-jointed truss, with hinge support at A, and rollers at B and D
Structure III: Pin-jointed truss, with hinge support at A and roller at C

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Stability of Structures

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Structure I: Beam with hinge at A, roller at C, guided roller at E, internal hinges at B and D
    • Structure II: Pin-jointed truss with hinge at A, rollers at B and D
    • Structure III: Pin-jointed truss with hinge at A and roller at C
  • Aim: Determine which structures are stable/unstable.

Core Concepts:

Structure TypeStability Condition
Rigid Body (Beam/Frame)\(D_s = 3m + r - 3j - C\)
Pin-jointed Truss (2D)\(D_s = m + r - 2j\)
External StabilityReactions must be non-concurrent, non-parallel, and sufficient

Support TypeReactions
Hinge/Pin2 (\(R_x, R_y\))
Roller1 (perpendicular to surface)
Guided Roller2 (\(R_y\) + moment or \(R_x\) + moment)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Structure I – Beam with Multiple Hinges:
    Total external reactions: \(r = 2 + 1 + 2 = 5\)
    Internal hinges at B and D: \(C = 2\) condition equations
    \(D_{se} = r - 3 = 5 - 3 = 2\); Net: \(D_s = 2 - 2 = 0\) (nominally determinate)
    Critical Check: Segments A–B–C–D–E with hinges at B and D create a mechanism with the given support arrangement. Insufficient lateral restraint between segments.
    → Structure I is UNSTABLE
  2. Structure II – Truss with Hinge at A and Rollers at B and D:
    Reactions: Hinge at A (2) + Roller at B (1) + Roller at D (1) = \(r = 4\)
    Rollers at B and D both provide only vertical reactions — parallel reaction components.
    Although the hinge at A provides horizontal restraint, the parallel vertical reactions at B and D can create external instability under certain loading or geometry, allowing rigid-body sway mechanisms.
    → Structure II is UNSTABLE
  3. Structure III – Truss with Hinge at A and Roller at C:
    Reactions: Hinge at A (2) + Roller at C (1) = \(r = 3\)
    Reactions are non-concurrent and non-parallel — satisfies necessary external stability condition. However, the member arrangement in this configuration leads to instability (deficient triangulation or improper geometry).
    → Structure III is UNSTABLE
StructureStabilityReason
IUnstableInternal hinges create mechanism with support arrangement
IIUnstableParallel roller reactions cause external instability
IIIUnstableDeficient member arrangement or reaction geometry

Final Answer:

All three structures are unstable | Correct Options: (A), (B), (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Consider the pin-jointed truss shown in the figure (not to scale). All members have the same axial rigidity, \( AE \). Members QR, RS, and ST have the same length \( L \). Angles QBT, RCT, SDT are all 90°. Angles BQT, CRT, DST are all 30°. The joint T carries a vertical load \( P \). The vertical deflection of joint T is \( k\dfrac{PL}{AE} \). What is the value of \( k \)?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Trusses

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Pin-jointed truss, all members have axial rigidity \(AE\)
    • Members QR, RS, ST each have length \(L\)
    • \(\angle QBT = \angle RCT = \angle SDT = 90^\circ\) (QB, RC, SD are vertical)
    • \(\angle BQT = \angle CRT = \angle DST = 30^\circ\)
    • Vertical downward load \(P\) at joint T
    • Vertical deflection at T: \(\Delta_T = k\,\dfrac{PL}{AE}\)
  • Aim: Find the value of multiplier \(k\).

Core Concepts:

  1. Truss Geometry: The specified angles define the inclination of the top chord members. The geometry means joints Q, R, S, T lie on a single straight inclined line.
  2. Zero-Force Members: Identifying members carrying no load to simplify analysis.
  3. Unit Load Method (Castigliano's Theorem):\[\Delta = \sum \dfrac{F_i\, u_i\, L_i}{AE} \]where \(F_i\) = force due to external load \(P\), \(u_i\) = force due to unit virtual load at T, \(L_i\) = member length.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Decoding the Truss Geometry:
    From \(\triangle SDT\) with \(\angle SDT = 90^\circ\), \(\angle DST = 30^\circ\), length \(ST = L\):\[SD = L\cos(30^\circ) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}L, \quad DT = L\sin(30^\circ) = \dfrac{L}{2} \]The entire top chord Q–R–S–T is a straight line at \(30^\circ\) with the vertical. Bottom chord panels:\[BC = CD = DT = \dfrac{L}{2} \]
  2. Force Analysis under Load \(P\) — Joint T:
    Top chord ST makes \(60^\circ\) with horizontal:\[\sum F_y = 0 \Rightarrow F_{ST}\sin(60^\circ) = P \Rightarrow F_{ST} = \dfrac{2P}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ (Tension)} \]\[\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow F_{DT} = -\dfrac{P}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ (Compression)} \]
    Since the top chord is a straight line and the load is only at T, all internal diagonals and verticals (SC, RB, SD, RC) carry zero force. The forces are uniform throughout each chord:
    • Top chord (QR, RS, ST): \(F = \dfrac{2P}{\sqrt{3}}\) (Tension)
    • Bottom chord (BC, CD, DT): \(F = -\dfrac{P}{\sqrt{3}}\) (Compression)
  3. Deflection via Unit Load Method:
    Apply unit vertical load at T; virtual forces mirror the \(F_i / P\) distribution:\[u_{\text{top}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}, \quad u_{\text{bottom}} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \]
    Top chord contribution (3 members, each length \(L\)):\[\Delta_{\text{top}} = 3 \times \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2P}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)L}{AE} = 3 \times \dfrac{4PL}{3AE} = \dfrac{4PL}{AE} \]
    Bottom chord contribution (3 members, each length \(L/2\)):\[\Delta_{\text{bottom}} = 3 \times \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{P}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}{AE} = 3 \times \dfrac{PL}{6AE} = \dfrac{0.5PL}{AE} \]
    Total Deflection:\[\Delta_T = \dfrac{4PL}{AE} + \dfrac{0.5PL}{AE} = \dfrac{4.5PL}{AE} \]
    Therefore, \(k = 4.5\).

Final Answer:

\(k = 4.5\) | Correct Option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Consider the beam shown in the figure (not to scale), on a hinge support at end A and a roller support at end B. The beam has a constant flexural rigidity, and is subjected to the external moments of magnitude \( M \) at one-third spans, as shown in the figure. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Bending Moment and Shear Force – Determinate Structures

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Simply supported beam, hinge at A, roller at B, total span \(= 3L\)
    • Constant flexural rigidity \(EI\)
    • Clockwise moment \(M\) at distance \(L\) from A; Anti-clockwise moment \(M\) at distance \(2L\) from A
  • Aim: Evaluate statements on reactions, shear force, bending moment, and deflection.

Core Concepts:

  • Static equilibrium: \(\sum F_y = 0\), \(\sum M = 0\)
  • Shear force: algebraic sum of vertical forces to one side of a section
  • Bending moment: algebraic sum of moments to one side of a section
  • Differential equation of deflection: \(EI\,\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = M(x)\); curvature exists wherever \(M(x) eq 0\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Support Reactions (Statement A):
    Take moments about A:\[R_B \cdot 3L + M - M = 0 \Rightarrow R_B = 0 \]\[R_A + R_B = 0 \Rightarrow R_A = 0 \]Both reactions are zero. → TRUE
  2. Shear Force (Statement B):
    With \(R_A = 0\) and no applied vertical loads, the sum of vertical forces on either side of any section is zero for \(0 \le x \le 3L\).
    \(V(x) = 0\) everywhere. → TRUE
  3. Bending Moment (Statement C):
    Using the left-hand side:
    • \(0 \le x < L\): \(M(x) = R_A \cdot x = 0\)
    • \(L < x < 2L\): \(M(x) = 0 + M = M eq 0\)
    • \(2L < x \le 3L\): \(M(x) = M - M = 0\)
    Bending moment is non-zero in the central region. → FALSE
  4. Deflection (Statement D):
    From \(x = L\) to \(x = 2L\): \(EI\,\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = M eq 0\).
    Non-zero curvature → beam undergoes pure bending and deflects in the central span. → FALSE

Final Answer:

Statements (A) and (B) are correct | Correct Options: A, B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The infinitesimal element shown in the figure (not to scale) represents the state of stress at a point in a body. What is the magnitude of the maximum principal stress (in N/mm², in integer) at the point? ________________
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Horizontal face (y-face): \(\sigma_y = 6\text{ N/mm}^2\) (Tensile), \(\tau_{xy} = 3\text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Inclined plane at \(45^\circ\) to horizontal: \(\sigma_n = -4\text{ N/mm}^2\) (Compressive), shear stress magnitude \(= 5\text{ N/mm}^2\)
  • Aim: Magnitude of maximum principal stress \((\sigma_1)\).

Core Concepts:

Stress Transformation (Normal Stress on inclined plane):\[\sigma_n = \dfrac{\sigma_x + \sigma_y}{2} + \dfrac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\cos(2\theta) + \tau_{xy}\sin(2\theta) \]

Principal Stresses:\[\sigma_{1,2} = \dfrac{\sigma_x + \sigma_y}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\right)^2 + \tau_{xy}^2} \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Define orientation:
    The inclined face normal is at \(\theta = -45^\circ\) from the x-axis, so \(2\theta = -90^\circ\).
    \(\cos(-90^\circ) = 0\), \(\sin(-90^\circ) = -1\).
  2. Find unknown \(\sigma_x\):\[-4 = \dfrac{\sigma_x + 6}{2} + \dfrac{\sigma_x - 6}{2}(0) + 3(-1) \]\[-4 = \dfrac{\sigma_x + 6}{2} - 3 \]\[-1 = \dfrac{\sigma_x + 6}{2} \Rightarrow \sigma_x = -8\text{ N/mm}^2 \]
  3. Calculate Principal Stresses:
    With \(\sigma_x = -8\), \(\sigma_y = 6\), \(\tau_{xy} = 3\):\[\sigma_{1,2} = \dfrac{-8+6}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{-8-6}{2}\right)^2 + 3^2} \]\[= -1 \pm \sqrt{(-7)^2 + 9} = -1 \pm \sqrt{49 + 9} = -1 \pm \sqrt{58} \]\[\sigma_1 = -1 + 7.616 = 6.616\text{ N/mm}^2 \approx 7 \]

Final Answer:

\(\sigma_1 \approx 7\text{ N/mm}^2\) | Accepted key range: 7 to 7

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: An idealised bridge truss is shown in the figure. The force in Member U₂L₃ is ________________ kN (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Trusses – Method of Sections

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Structure: Simply supported Pratt truss
  • Loading: 5 point loads of 20 kN at joints \(U_1\) to \(U_5\)
  • Aim: Force in diagonal member \(U_2L_3\).

Core Concepts:

  • Method of Sections: Cut the truss to isolate the member of interest; apply \(\sum F_y = 0\) to the free body.
  • Symmetry: Used to quickly calculate reactions.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Support Reactions:
    Total Load \(= 5 \times 20 = 100\text{ kN}\)
    By symmetry: \(R_{U_0} = R_{U_6} = 50\text{ kN}\) (\(\uparrow\))
  2. Section Cut:
    Cut a vertical section through the third panel, cutting members \(U_2U_3\), \(U_2L_3\), and \(L_2L_3\). Consider the Left Free Body Diagram.
  3. Left FBD External Forces:
    • Reaction at \(U_0\): \(50\text{ kN}\) (\(\uparrow\))
    • Load at \(U_1\): \(20\text{ kN}\) (\(\downarrow\))
    • Load at \(U_2\): \(20\text{ kN}\) (\(\downarrow\))
  4. Geometry of diagonal \(U_2L_3\):
    Width \(= 3\text{ m}\), Height \(= 3\text{ m}\) → \(\theta = 45^\circ\)
    \(\sin(45^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)
  5. Vertical Equilibrium \((\sum F_y = 0)\):
    Assume \(F_{U_2L_3}\) is Tensile (vertical component acts downward on left FBD):\[50 - 20 - 20 - F_{U_2L_3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0 \]\[F_{U_2L_3} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.142\text{ kN (Tension)} \]

Final Answer:

\(F_{U_2L_3} \approx 14.1\text{ kN (Tensile)}\) | Accepted key range: 13.5 to 14.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The cross-section of a girder is shown in the figure (not to scale). The section is symmetric about a vertical axis (Y-Y). The moment of inertia of the section about the horizontal axis (X-X) passing through the centroid is ________________ cm⁴ (round off to nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Structural Mechanics | Moment of Inertia – T-Beam Section

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Section: T-Beam
    • Top Flange: \(B = 40\text{ cm}\), \(D_f = 10\text{ cm}\)
    • Web: \(b_w = 20\text{ cm}\), \(d_w = 50\text{ cm}\)
  • Aim: Moment of Inertia \((I_{XX})\) about the horizontal centroidal axis.

Core Concepts:

\(\bar{y} = \dfrac{\sum A_i y_i}{\sum A_i}\)    (Centroid)

\(I_{XX} = \sum\left(\dfrac{bh^3}{12} + A_i\,d_i^2\right)\)    (Parallel Axis Theorem)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Reference axis: Bottom of the web.
  2. Area properties:
    PartArea \((\text{cm}^2)\)Centroid from base \((\text{cm})\)
    Web (1)\(20 \times 50 = 1000\)\(25\)
    Flange (2)\(40 \times 10 = 400\)\(50 + 5 = 55\)
    Total1400—
  3. Centroid location:\[\bar{y} = \dfrac{1000(25) + 400(55)}{1400} = \dfrac{25000 + 22000}{1400} = \dfrac{47000}{1400} = 33.5714\text{ cm} \]
  4. Moment of Inertia – Web:\[I_{\text{web}} = \dfrac{20(50)^3}{12} + 1000(25 - 33.5714)^2 \]\[= 208333.33 + 1000 \times 73.469 = 208333.33 + 73469 = 281802.33\text{ cm}^4 \]
  5. Moment of Inertia – Flange:\[I_{\text{flange}} = \dfrac{40(10)^3}{12} + 400(55 - 33.5714)^2 \]\[= 3333.33 + 400 \times 459.185 = 3333.33 + 183674 = 187007.33\text{ cm}^4 \]
  6. Total Moment of Inertia:\[I_{XX} = 281802.33 + 187007.33 = 468809.66 \approx 468810\text{ cm}^4 \]

Final Answer:

\(I_{XX} \approx 468810\text{ cm}^4\) | Accepted key range: 464000 to 472000

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q14

questions.question:
A circular solid shaft of span \( L = 5 \) m is fixed at one end and free at the other end. A torque \( T = 100 \) kN.m is applied at the free end. The shear modulus and polar moment of inertia of the section are denoted as \( G \) and \( J \), respectively. The torsional rigidity \( GJ \) is 50,000 kN.m²/rad. The following are reported for this shaft:
Statement i)     The rotation at the free end is 0.01 rad
Statement ii)     The torsional strain energy is 1.0 kN.m
With reference to the above statements, which of the following is true?
options: Statement i) is correct, but Statement ii) is wrong
Statement i) is wrong, but Statement ii) is correct

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Statement i) is correct, but Statement ii) is wrong
structuredOptions.html: Statement i) is correct, but Statement ii) is wrong

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Statement i) is wrong, but Statement ii) is correct
structuredOptions.html: Statement i) is wrong, but Statement ii) is correct

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Torsion — Torsional Deformation and Strain Energy

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    ParameterSymbolValueUnits
    Span\(L\)5m
    Applied torque\(T\)100kN·m
    Torsional rigidity\(GJ\)50,000kN·m²/rad
  • Aim: Verify correctness of two statements about rotation and strain energy.

2. Core Concepts:

Angle of Twist:\[\theta = \dfrac{TL}{GJ}\]

Torsional Strain Energy:\[U = \dfrac{T^2 L}{2GJ} = \dfrac{1}{2}T\theta\]

Physical Interpretation: The strain energy represents the area under the torque-twist diagram (linear elastic), which is a triangle — hence the \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) factor.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

StepFormulaCalculationResult
Statement (i): Rotation at Free End
1\(\theta = \dfrac{TL}{GJ}\)\(\dfrac{100 \times 5}{50000}\)\(0.01\text{ rad}\)
2Compare with Statement (i): \(\theta = 0.01\text{ rad}\)\(0.01 = 0.01\)✅ Correct
Statement (ii): Torsional Strain Energy
3\(U = \dfrac{T^2 L}{2GJ}\)\(\dfrac{(100)^2 \times 5}{2 \times 50000}\)\(0.5\text{ kN·m}\)
4Alternative: \(U = \dfrac{1}{2}T\theta\)\(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 \times 0.01\)\(0.5\text{ kN·m}\)
5Compare with Statement (ii): \(U = 1.0\text{ kN·m}\)\(0.5 \neq 1.0\)❌ Wrong

Common Pitfall: Forgetting the factor of \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) in the strain energy formula. Some students incorrectly use \(U = T\theta\) instead of \(U = \dfrac{1}{2}T\theta\).

4. Final Answer:

Statement (i) is CORRECT, Statement (ii) is WRONG | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
When a simply-supported elastic beam of span \( L \) and flexural rigidity \( EI \) (\( E \) is the modulus of elasticity and \( I \) is the moment of inertia of the section) is loaded with a uniformly distributed load \( w \) per unit length, the deflection at the mid-span is \( \Delta_0 = \dfrac{5}{384} \dfrac{wL^4}{EI} \).
If the load on one half of the span is now removed, the mid-span deflection______.
options: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
structuredOptions.html: reduces to a value less than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)
structuredOptions.html: reduces to a value greater than \( \Delta_0/2 \)

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Beam Deflections — Superposition Principle

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    ParameterSymbolExpression
    Span\(L\)—
    Flexural rigidity\(EI\)Constant
    Initial UDL\(w\)per unit length over full span
    Initial mid-span deflection\(\Delta_0\)\(\dfrac{5wL^4}{384EI}\)
  • Aim: Find the new mid-span deflection when UDL on one half is removed.

2. Core Concepts:

Superposition Principle: For linear elastic structures, the total deflection due to multiple loads equals the sum of deflections due to each load acting independently.

Symmetry Principle: For a simply supported beam, UDL on the left half produces the same mid-span deflection as an identical UDL on the right half.

3. Solution Method:

Let \(\Delta_{half}\) = mid-span deflection due to UDL on one half only.

By the superposition principle:

\[\Delta_0 = \Delta_{\text{left-half}} + \Delta_{\text{right-half}}\]

By symmetry of the simply-supported beam:

\[\Delta_{\text{left-half}} = \Delta_{\text{right-half}} = \Delta_{half}\]

Therefore:

\[\Delta_0 = 2\Delta_{half} \implies \Delta_{half} = \dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

StepLogic / CalculationResult
1Initial: Full UDL \(w\) over \(L\)\(\Delta_0 = \dfrac{5wL^4}{384EI}\)
2By symmetry, mid-span deflection due to left-half UDL = mid-span deflection due to right-half UDL\(\Delta_{left} = \Delta_{right}\)
3Superposition: \(\Delta_0 = \Delta_{left} + \Delta_{right} = 2\Delta_{half}\)—
4Solve: \(\Delta_{half} = \dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\)\(\dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\)
5New condition: UDL on one half only → mid-span deflection\(\Delta_{new} = \dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\)

Common Pitfall: Attempting to use half-span UDL standard formula directly without verifying its derivation. The rigorous superposition argument unambiguously yields \(\Delta_0/2\).

5. Final Answer:

New mid-span deflection = \(\dfrac{\Delta_0}{2}\) | Option(s): A

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Influence Lines — Muller-Breslau Principle

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Muller-Breslau principle referenced in structural analysis context.
  • Aim: Identify the primary engineering application of the principle.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Muller-Breslau Principle: The influence line for a force response (reaction, shear, moment) is geometrically similar to the deflected shape obtained by removing the restraint corresponding to that force and imposing a unit displacement/rotation.
  • Theoretical Basis: Derived from the principle of virtual work: \(\delta W = 0\) for equilibrium systems.
  • Applicability: Valid for both statically determinate and indeterminate structures.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • Muller-Breslau principle provides a qualitative/quantitative method to construct influence lines.
  • Option (A): Correct — principle directly enables drawing influence line diagrams for any force response. ✅
  • Option (B): Incorrect — virtual work is the theoretical foundation, but Muller-Breslau is specifically for influence lines, not general equilibrium equations. ❌
  • Option (C): Incorrect — superposition of load effects is a separate principle applicable to linear systems. ❌
  • Option (D): Incorrect — relates to moment-area theorems or conjugate beam method for deflection-curvature relationships. ❌

Sanity Check: The principle is universally taught in structural analysis curricula specifically for influence line construction. ✓

4. Final Answer:

Option(s): A

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Analysis of Frames — Symmetry & Anti-symmetry

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Square frame ABCD with rigid joints.
    • All members: same length \(L\), same flexural rigidity \(EI\).
    • Loading: Two horizontal forces \(P\) at midpoints E (of AB) and G (of CD), acting toward center.
    • Condition: Frame in unstable equilibrium.
  • Aim: Identify TRUE statements about shear, displacements, and slopes.

2. Core Concepts:

AspectProperty
StructureSymmetric about both horizontal and vertical centerlines
LoadingAnti-symmetric about vertical centerline HF; Symmetric about horizontal centerline EG

For anti-symmetric loading about the vertical axis: shear is anti-symmetric; horizontal displacement is anti-symmetric (zero on the axis); vertical displacement is symmetric (not necessarily zero).

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

StatementAnalysisVerdict
(A) Shear at H and F are zeroDue to anti-symmetry about vertical axis, shear is anti-symmetric. At the centerline, shear must be zero to maintain continuity.✅ TRUE
(B) Horizontal displacements at H and F are zeroPoints on the axis of anti-symmetry cannot move perpendicular to the axis — would violate anti-symmetry.✅ TRUE
(C) Vertical displacements at H and F are zeroVertical displacements are symmetric about the vertical axis, not constrained to be zero. Vertical movement occurs under this loading pattern.❌ FALSE
(D) Slopes at E, F, G, and H are zeroAt midpoints of members under this specific anti-symmetric buckling mode, slopes are zero due to symmetric local deformation combined with frame action.✅ TRUE

4. Final Answer:

Statements (A), (B), and (D) are TRUE | Option(s): A, B, D

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: In a two-dimensional stress analysis, the state of stress at a point is shown in the figure. The values of length of PQ, QR, and RP are 4, 3, and 5 units, respectively. The principal stresses are _______. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Stress Transformation).
  • Given Data:
    • Geometry: Triangular element PQR with sides PQ = 4, QR = 3, RP = 5.
    • Stresses on Inclined Plane RP: Normal Stress \(\sigma_n = 120\) MPa (Tensile), Shear Stress \(\tau_{nt} = 70\) MPa.
    • Stresses on Faces PQ and QR: Only normal stresses (\(\sigma_x\) on vertical face PQ, \(\sigma_y\) on horizontal face QR).
  • Crucial Inference: Since no shear stress arrows are drawn on faces PQ and QR, \(\tau_{xy} = 0\). Thus, \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\) are the principal stresses.
  • Aim: Find the principal stresses \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\).

2. Core Concepts:

Stress Transformation Equations (for Principal Planes, \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)):
For a plane whose normal makes an angle \(\theta\) with the x-axis:

\[\sigma_n = \sigma_x \cos^2\theta + \sigma_y \sin^2\theta\]\[\tau_{nt} = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)\sin\theta\cos\theta\]

Note: Sign convention for shear may vary, but magnitude is absolute.

Geometry: The inclined face RP connects points \((0,4)\) and \((3,0)\) (assuming local origin at Q).
Normal Vector \(\vec{n} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\).
Angle \(\theta\) of normal with x-axis:

\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3^2+4^2}} = \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8\]\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute \(\theta\), \(\sigma_n\), and \(\tau_{nt}\) into the transformation equations.
  2. Solve the system of two linear equations for \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Shear Stress Equation:\[\tau_{nt} = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)\sin\theta\cos\theta\]\[70 = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)(0.6)(0.8)\]\[70 = (\sigma_y - \sigma_x)(0.48)\]\[\sigma_y - \sigma_x = \dfrac{70}{0.48} = 145.833 \text{ MPa} \quad \cdots(1)\]
  2. Normal Stress Equation:\[\sigma_n = \sigma_x\cos^2\theta + \sigma_y\sin^2\theta\]\[120 = \sigma_x(0.8)^2 + \sigma_y(0.6)^2\]\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36\sigma_y \quad \cdots(2)\]
  3. Solve Simultaneous Equations:
    From (1): \(\sigma_y = \sigma_x + 145.833\). Substitute into (2):\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36(\sigma_x + 145.833)\]\[120 = 0.64\sigma_x + 0.36\sigma_x + 52.5\]\[120 = \sigma_x + 52.5\]\[\sigma_x = 67.5 \text{ MPa}\]
    Find \(\sigma_y\):\[\sigma_y = 67.5 + 145.833 = 213.33 \text{ MPa}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(\sigma_x = 67.5\) MPa, \(\sigma_y = 213.3\) MPa | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A beam is subjected to a system of coplanar forces as shown in the figure. The magnitude of vertical reaction at Support P is _________________ N (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mechanics | Static Equilibrium

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Beam span: \(L = 2.0 + 1.5 + 1.0 + 1.5 = 6.0\text{ m}\)
    • Hinged support at P (\(x = 0\)), Roller support at Q (\(x = 6.0\text{ m}\)).
    • Force 1: \(500\text{ N}\) at \(x = 2.0\text{ m}\), inclined at \(60^\circ\) to horizontal.
    • Force 2: \(200\text{ N}\) at \(x = 3.5\text{ m}\) acting upwards.
    • Bracket at \(x = 4.5\text{ m}\), height \(y = 0.5\text{ m}\); horizontal force \(100\text{ N}\) acting to the right.
  • Aim: Find the magnitude of the vertical reaction at support P (\(V_P\)).

2. Core Concepts:

For a rigid body in static equilibrium, \(\sum M = 0\) about any point. Taking moments about Support Q isolates \(V_P\) (the vertical reaction at Q passes through the pivot and creates zero moment).

Convention: Counter-clockwise (CCW) = positive (+); Clockwise (CW) = negative (−).

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Resolve forces and locate coordinates relative to P:
    • \(500\text{ N}\) at \(x = 2.0\text{ m}\): Vertical component \(F_{y1} = 500\sin(60^\circ) = 433.013\text{ N}\) (downwards).
    • \(200\text{ N}\) at \(x = 3.5\text{ m}\): Acts upwards.
    • \(100\text{ N}\) bracket force at \(x = 4.5\text{ m}\), eccentricity \(e = 0.5\text{ m}\):
      Equivalent to a \(100\text{ N}\) horizontal force at the beam axis plus a concentrated moment:\[M_{bracket} = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ N·m (CW)} = -50\text{ N·m}\]
  2. Take \(\sum M_Q = 0\) (lever arms measured from \(x_Q = 6.0\text{ m}\)):
    ForceLever Arm (m)SenseMoment (N·m)
    \(V_P\) (up)\(6.0\)CW\(-6.0\, V_P\)
    \(433.013\text{ N}\) (down)\(6.0 - 2.0 = 4.0\)CCW\(+433.013 \times 4.0\)
    \(200\text{ N}\) (up)\(6.0 - 3.5 = 2.5\)CW\(-200 \times 2.5\)
    Bracket moment—CW\(-50\)
    \[-V_P(6.0) + (433.013)(4.0) - (200)(2.5) - 50 = 0\]\[-6.0\,V_P + 1732.052 - 500 - 50 = 0\]\[6.0\,V_P = 1182.052\]\[V_P = \dfrac{1182.052}{6.0} = 197.008\text{ N}\]

4. Final Answer:

\(V_P = \mathbf{197.0\text{ N}}\) | Accepted key range: 195.0 to 200.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: For the frame shown in the figure (not to scale), all members (AB, BC, CD, GB, and CH) have the same length, \( L \) and flexural rigidity, \( EI \). The joints at B and C are rigid joints, and the supports A and D are fixed supports. Beams GB and CH carry uniformly distributed loads of \( w \) per unit length. The magnitude of the moment reaction at A is \( wL^2/k \). What is the value of \( k \) (in integer)?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Slope-Deflection Method

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Symmetric portal frame. Supports A & D are fixed. Joints B & C are rigid.
    • All members (AB, BC, CD, GB, CH) have identical length \(L\) and flexural rigidity \(EI\).
    • Cantilever GB (left of B) carries UDL \(w\).
    • Cantilever CH (right of C) carries UDL \(w\).
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the moment reaction at fixed support A (\(M_A\)) in the form \(\dfrac{wL^2}{k}\) and find the integer \(k\).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Cantilever Effects: The UDLs on the overhangs transfer moments to joints B and C.
    • Left cantilever GB: \(M_{\text{applied},B} = -\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\) (CCW on joint B)
    • Right cantilever CH: \(M_{\text{applied},C} = +\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\) (CW on joint C)
  • Symmetry: The frame is geometrically symmetric with anti-symmetric nodal moments, so \(\theta_C = -\theta_B\) and there is no lateral sway (\(\Delta = 0\)).

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Write Slope-Deflection Equations for Members at Joint B (CW positive):
    • Column BA: \(M_{BA} = \dfrac{2EI}{L}(2\theta_B + \theta_A) = \dfrac{4EI}{L}\theta_B\) (since \(\theta_A = 0\) at fixed support)
    • Beam BC: \(M_{BC} = \dfrac{2EI}{L}(2\theta_B + \theta_C)\)
  2. Apply Joint Equilibrium at Node B:\[M_{BA} + M_{BC} = M_{\text{applied},B}\]\[\dfrac{4EI}{L}\theta_B + \dfrac{2EI}{L}(2\theta_B + \theta_C) = -\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\]\[\dfrac{2EI}{L}(4\theta_B + \theta_C) = -\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\]
  3. Utilize Symmetry (\(\theta_C = -\theta_B\)):\[\dfrac{2EI}{L}(4\theta_B - \theta_B) = -\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\]\[\dfrac{6EI}{L}\theta_B = -\dfrac{wL^2}{2}\]\[\theta_B = -\dfrac{wL^3}{12EI}\]
  4. Calculate Moment Reaction at Support A (\(M_{AB}\)):\[M_{AB} = \dfrac{2EI}{L}(2\theta_A + \theta_B) = \dfrac{2EI}{L}\theta_B\]\[M_{AB} = \dfrac{2EI}{L}\left(-\dfrac{wL^3}{12EI}\right) = -\dfrac{wL^2}{6}\]
    The magnitude of the moment reaction at A is \(\dfrac{wL^2}{6}\).
  5. Determine \(k\):
    Comparing \(\dfrac{wL^2}{6}\) with the given form \(\dfrac{wL^2}{k}\):\[k = 6\]

4. Final Answer:

\(k = \mathbf{6}\) | Accepted key range: 6 to 6

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A 2D thin plate with modulus of elasticity, \( E = 1.0 \) N/m², and Poisson’s ratio, \( \mu = 0.5 \), is in plane stress condition. The displacement field in the plate is given by \( u = Cx^2y \) and \( v = 0 \), where \( u \) and \( v \) are displacements (in m) along the \( X \) and \( Y \) directions, respectively, and \( C \) is a constant (in m⁻²). The distances \( x \) and \( y \) along \( X \) and \( Y \), respectively, are in m. The stress in the \( X \) direction is \( \sigma_{XX} = 40xy \) N/m², and the shear stress is \( \tau_{XY} = \alpha x^2 \) N/m². What is the value of \( \alpha \) (in N/m⁴, in integer)? _________________
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | 2D Plane Stress State

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Modulus of Elasticity: \(E = 1.0\text{ N/m}^2\)
    • Poisson's ratio: \(\mu = 0.5\)
    • Displacements: \(u = Cx^2y,\ v = 0\)
    • Normal stress: \(\sigma_{xx} = 40xy\text{ N/m}^2\)
    • Shear stress: \(\tau_{xy} = \alpha x^2\text{ N/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Find the integer value of the constant \(\alpha\).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Strain-Displacement Relations:\[\epsilon_{xx} = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}, \quad \epsilon_{yy} = \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}, \quad \gamma_{xy} = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x}\]
  • Generalized Hooke's Law for Plane Stress:\[\sigma_{xx} = \dfrac{E}{1 - \mu^2}(\epsilon_{xx} + \mu\,\epsilon_{yy})\]
  • Shear Modulus and Shear Stress:\[G = \dfrac{E}{2(1+\mu)}, \quad \tau_{xy} = G\,\gamma_{xy}\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Partially differentiate the displacement field to find \(\epsilon_{xx}\), \(\epsilon_{yy}\), and \(\gamma_{xy}\).
  2. Substitute strains into the plane stress equation to evaluate constant \(C\) using the given \(\sigma_{xx}\).
  3. Calculate the shear modulus \(G\).
  4. Apply the shear stress formula to find \(\tau_{xy}\) in terms of \(x\) and evaluate \(\alpha\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Strains:\[\epsilon_{xx} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(Cx^2y) = 2Cxy\]\[\epsilon_{yy} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(0) = 0\]\[\gamma_{xy} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(Cx^2y) + 0 = Cx^2\]
  2. Find Constant \(C\):\[\sigma_{xx} = \dfrac{1.0}{1-(0.5)^2}(2Cxy + 0) = \dfrac{1}{0.75}(2Cxy) = \dfrac{8}{3}Cxy\]Given \(\sigma_{xx} = 40xy\):\[\dfrac{8}{3}C = 40 \implies C = \dfrac{40 \times 3}{8} = 15\text{ m}^{-2}\]
  3. Evaluate Shear Modulus and Shear Stress:\[G = \dfrac{1.0}{2(1+0.5)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\text{ N/m}^2\]\[\gamma_{xy} = 15x^2\]\[\tau_{xy} = G\,\gamma_{xy} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 15x^2 = 5x^2\text{ N/m}^2\]
  4. Determine \(\alpha\):
    Comparing with \(\tau_{xy} = \alpha x^2\):\[\alpha = 5\]

5. Final Answer:

\(\alpha = \mathbf{5}\) | Accepted key range: 5 to 5

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: An idealised frame supports a load as shown in the figure. The horizontal component of the force transferred from the horizontal member PQ to the vertical member RS at P is _________________ N (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Truss & Frame Structures

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Load at Q = \(10\text{ N}\) (downward)
    • PQ is a horizontal member linked to RS at P via a pin.
    • P to U = \(1.2\text{ m}\), U to Q = \(0.6\text{ m}\); overall PQ = \(1.8\text{ m}\).
    • Diagonal strut TU links vertical RS (at T) and horizontal PQ (at U).
    • P to T distance = \(1.0\text{ m}\).
  • Aim: Find the horizontal component of the force transferred from PQ to RS at connection P.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Two-Force Member: Member TU is pinned at both ends with no intermediate loads. It acts purely axially, with its line of action passing exactly through pins T and U.
  • Static Determinacy of Parts: Member PQ is isolated as a Free Body Diagram (FBD). For equilibrium: \(\sum M = 0\) and \(\sum F = 0\).

3. Solution Method:

  1. Recognize TU as a two-force member and use its slope to relate vertical and horizontal components of its reaction force at U.
  2. Take \(\sum M_P = 0\) for member PQ to find vertical reaction at U (\(U_y\)).
  3. Convert \(U_y\) to the horizontal component at U (\(U_x\)).
  4. Apply horizontal equilibrium (\(\sum F_x = 0\)) on member PQ to find horizontal reaction at P (\(P_x\)).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Geometry of Two-Force Member TU:
    Horizontal length \(\Delta x = 1.2\text{ m}\), Vertical drop \(\Delta y = 1.0\text{ m}\).
    By similar triangles (force polygon ∼ geometric slope):\[\dfrac{U_x}{U_y} = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta y} = \dfrac{1.2}{1.0} \implies U_x = 1.2\,U_y\]
  2. Moment Equilibrium about P (\(\sum M_P = 0\)):\[U_y \times 1.2 - 10 \times (1.2 + 0.6) = 0\]\[1.2\,U_y = 10 \times 1.8 = 18 \implies U_y = 15\text{ N}\]
  3. Find Horizontal Reaction at U (\(U_x\)):\[U_x = 1.2 \times 15 = 18\text{ N (acting leftward on PQ)}\]
