  1. Base SI unit assignment:\[k = 4\pi^2\text{ kN/m} = 4000\pi^2\text{ N/m}, \qquad m = 10\text{ kg} \]
  2. Angular Frequency (\(\omega_n\)):\[\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{4000\pi^2}{10}} = \sqrt{400\pi^2} = 20\pi\text{ rad/s} \]
  3. Cyclic Frequency (\(f_n\)):\[f_n = \dfrac{20\pi}{2\pi} = 10\text{ Hz} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10 Hz | Accepted key range: 10 to 10

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A perfectly flexible and inextensible cable is shown in the figure (not to scale). The external loads at F and G are acting vertically.



The magnitude of tension in the cable segment FG (in kN, round off to two decimal places) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Point Loaded Cables

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Supports at E and H. H is \(1\text{ m}\) below E (\(y_H = -1\text{ m}\)).
    • Total horizontal span = \(6\text{ m}\); nodes E, F, G, H are spaced \(2\text{ m}\) apart horizontally.
    • Vertical depth of F from E: \(y_F = -3\text{ m}\)
    • Point loads: \(W_F = 10\text{ kN}\) downwards, \(W_G = 12\text{ kN}\) downwards.
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the tension in cable segment FG (in kN).

3. Core Concepts:

Funicular Cable Properties: A perfectly flexible cable strictly carries axial tension.

Constant Horizontal Component: Without horizontal external loads, the horizontal component of tension (\(H\)) is constant across all segments.

Global Equilibrium: \(\sum M = 0\) about any support applies to the entire structure.

Segmental Equilibrium (Method of Sections): Cutting the cable and taking moments about a node for one side must equal zero.

Node Equilibrium: Applying \(\sum F_x = 0\) and \(\sum F_y = 0\) at any node relates segment tensions.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define coordinate geometry with origin at E\((0,0)\). Thus \(F(2,-3)\) and \(H(6,-1)\).
  2. Apply global moment equilibrium about H to get an equation linking \(V_E\) and \(H\).
  3. Isolate the left portion (EF) and apply moment equilibrium about F for a second equation.
  4. Solve simultaneously to get \(V_E\) and \(H\).
  5. Isolate node F to determine the vertical component of tension (\(V_{FG}\)) in segment FG.
  6. Calculate total tension: \(T_{FG} = \sqrt{H^2 + V_{FG}^2}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Global Equilibrium about H (\(\sum M_H = 0\)):\[V_E \cdot 6 - H \cdot 1 - 10 \times 4 - 12 \times 2 = 0 \]\[6V_E - H - 64 = 0 \quad \cdots\text{(Eq. 1)} \]
  2. Sectional Equilibrium about F — left side (\(\sum M_F = 0\)):\[V_E \cdot 2 - H \cdot 3 = 0 \implies V_E = 1.5H \quad \cdots\text{(Eq. 2)} \]
  3. Solve for reactions:
    Substituting Eq. 2 into Eq. 1:\[6(1.5H) - H = 64 \implies 8H = 64 \implies H = 8\text{ kN} \]\[V_E = 1.5 \times 8 = 12\text{ kN} \]
  4. Node F Equilibrium & Tension in FG:
    Vertical upward pull from EF on node F = \(V_E = 12\text{ kN}\).
    Downward external load at F = \(10\text{ kN}\).
    Let \(V_{FG}\) = downward vertical component of FG on node F:\[\sum F_y = 0: \quad 12 - 10 - V_{FG} = 0 \implies V_{FG} = 2\text{ kN} \]
  5. Resultant Tension in FG:\[T_{FG} = \sqrt{H^2 + V_{FG}^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{64 + 4} = \sqrt{68} \approx 8.246\text{ kN} \]

Sanity Check on Cable Profile: Drop from F to G = \((2/8)\times 2 = 0.5\text{ m}\), so \(y_G = -3.5\text{ m}\). At G: \(V_{GH} = 12 - 2 = 10\text{ kN}\) upward. Rise from G to H = \((10/8)\times 2 = 2.5\text{ m}\), giving \(y_H = -3.5 + 2.5 = -1.0\text{ m}\). This exactly matches the given boundary condition \(y_H = -1\text{ m}\). ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.25 kN | Accepted key range: 8.10 to 8.40

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Consider the planar truss shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale)



Neglecting self-weight of the members, the number of zero-force members in the truss under the action of the load \(P\), is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Trusses / Zero-Force Members

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A planar truss with 11 members (including the vertical wall member). External load \(P\) at the first bottom node.
  • Aim: Find the total number of zero-force members.

3. Core Concepts:

Rule 1 (Two-Member Joint): If two non-collinear members meet at an unloaded joint, both carry zero force.

Rule 2 (Three-Member Joint): If three members meet at an unloaded joint and two are collinear, the third (non-collinear) member carries zero force.

Kinematic Constraint Rule: A member connecting two absolutely fixed support points experiences zero strain → zero force.

Nomenclature: Top nodes: \(U_0\) (wall), \(U_1\), \(U_2\), \(U_3\) (free tip). Bottom nodes: \(L_0\) (wall), \(L_1\) (loaded), \(L_2\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Starting from the unloaded free end (\(U_3\)) and working backward:

StepJointReasoningZero-Force MembersRunning Count
1\(U_3\)Members \(U_2U_3\) and \(L_2U_3\) meet; no external load → Rule 1\(U_2U_3\), \(L_2U_3\)2
2\(L_2\)\(L_2U_3 = 0\); remaining \(L_1L_2\) and \(U_2L_2\); no load → Rule 1\(L_1L_2\), \(U_2L_2\)4
3\(U_2\)\(U_2U_3 = 0\), \(U_2L_2 = 0\); remaining \(U_1U_2\) and \(L_1U_2\); no load → Rule 1\(U_1U_2\), \(L_1U_2\)6
4\(L_1\)\(L_1L_2 = 0\), \(L_1U_2 = 0\); load \(P\) acts downward; \(\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow F_{L_0L_1} = 0\); \(F_{U_1L_1} = P\) (active)\(L_0L_1\)7
5Wall member\(U_0L_0\) connects two fixed supports; \(\Delta L = 0 \Rightarrow \epsilon = 0 \Rightarrow F = 0\)\(U_0L_0\)8

Active Members: Only the triangle \(U_0\)-\(U_1\)-\(L_0\) and the vertical tie \(U_1\)-\(L_1\) carry load \(P\) (3 active members out of 11).

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8 zero-force members | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
In a two-dimensional stress analysis, the state of stress at a point \(P\) is

\[[\sigma] = \begin{bmatrix} \sigma_{xx} & \tau_{xy} \\ \tau_{xy} & \sigma_{yy} \end{bmatrix}\]

The necessary and sufficient condition for existence of the state of pure shear at the point \(P\), is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses and Strains

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A generic 2D stress tensor:\[ [\sigma] = \begin{bmatrix} \sigma_{xx} & \tau_{xy} \\ \tau_{xy} & \sigma_{yy} \end{bmatrix} \]
  • Aim: State the necessary and sufficient condition for a pure shear state at point P.

3. Core Concepts:

Pure Shear State: A stress state where there exist mutually perpendicular planes with only shear stresses (normal stresses = 0). On Mohr's circle, the center lies at the origin, meaning \(\sigma_1 + \sigma_2 = 0\).

First Stress Invariant: The trace of the stress tensor is invariant under axis rotation:\[I_1 = \sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy} = \sigma_1 + \sigma_2 \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. For pure shear: \(\sigma_1 + \sigma_2 = 0\).
  2. By stress invariant: \(\sigma_1 + \sigma_2 = \sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy}\).
  3. Therefore the required condition is: \(\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy} = 0\).

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy} = 0\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: During the process of hydration of cement, due to increase in Dicalcium Silicate (C₂S) content in cement clinker, the heat of hydration
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Cement

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Increasing content of Dicalcium Silicate (\(C_2S\)) in cement clinker.
  • Aim: Determine the effect on the overall heat of hydration.

3. Core Concepts:

Bogue's Compounds and Heat of Hydration:

CompoundReaction RateHeat of Hydration
\(C_3A\)Very fastVery high
\(C_3S\)FastHigh
\(C_2S\)SlowLowest
\(C_4AF\)ModerateLow

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Increasing \(C_2S\) proportionally replaces faster-reacting components (\(C_3S\), \(C_3A\)).
  2. Since \(C_2S\) releases substantially less heat per gram, the aggregate heat of hydration decreases.
  3. This is the working principle behind Low Heat Portland Cement.

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Decreases | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A planar elastic structure is subjected to uniformly distributed load, as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale)



Neglecting self-weight, the maximum bending moment generated in the structure (in kN.m, round off to the nearest integer), is _________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Arches and Curved Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Requires critical observation of visual data over blind formula application)
  • Given Data:
    • Uniformly distributed load: \(w = 12\) kN/m
    • Horizontal span: \(L = 8.0\) m
    • Central rise of parabolic profile: \(h = 2.4\) m
    • Left support: Pinned/Hinged
    • Right support: Roller
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum bending moment generated in the structure (kN·m).

Sanity Check & Error Handling:

At first glance, this resembles a classic parabolic arch problem. In a true two-hinged or three-hinged arch under full UDL, the horizontal thrust perfectly balances the beam moment, resulting in zero bending moment everywhere. However, the roller support on the right cannot resist horizontal forces. Therefore, no horizontal thrust (\(H = 0\)) can develop, and the structure acts purely as a simply supported curved beam.

3. Core Concepts:

General Bending Moment in a Curved Structure:\[M_x = M_{beam} - H \cdot y \]where \(M_{beam}\) is the BM assuming a straight simply supported beam, \(H\) is horizontal thrust, and \(y\) is the arch height at that section.

Support Conditions:

  • Pinned support: provides both vertical (\(V\)) and horizontal (\(H\)) reactions.
  • Roller support: provides only vertical (\(V\)) reaction → \(H = 0\).

Maximum BM for Simply Supported Beam under Full UDL:\[M_{max} = \dfrac{wL^2}{8} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Use static equilibrium to determine vertical and horizontal reactions.
  2. Identify that the roller support dictates \(H = 0\).
  3. Calculate the peak bending moment at mid-span as for a straight simply supported beam.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Horizontal Reactions

Support B is a roller: \(H_B = 0\).
Horizontal equilibrium:\[\sum F_x = 0 \implies H_A = H_B = 0 \]Conclusion: Zero horizontal thrust in the structure.

Step 2: Vertical Reactions

By symmetry of structure and loading:

\[V_A = V_B = \dfrac{wL}{2} = \dfrac{12 \times 8.0}{2} = 48 \text{ kN} \]

Step 3: Bending Moment Equation at Section x

\[M_x = V_A \cdot x - w \cdot \dfrac{x^2}{2} - H_A \cdot y \]Substituting \(V_A = 48\) kN and \(H_A = 0\):\[M_x = 48x - 6x^2 \]

Step 4: Maximum Bending Moment

Maximize by differentiation:

\[\dfrac{dM_x}{dx} = 48 - 12x = 0 \implies x = 4 \text{ m (mid-span)} \]\[M_{max} = 48(4) - 6(4)^2 = 192 - 96 = \mathbf{96 \text{ kN·m}} \]

Note: The parabolic profile rise \(h = 2.4\) m is redundant distractor data, designed to mislead candidates into applying standard arch thrust formulas. Since \(H = 0\), the rise plays no role in the moment calculation.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 96 kN·m | Accepted key range: 95 to 97

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Distributed load(s) of 50 kN/m may occupy any position(s) (either continuously or in patches) on the girder PQRST as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale)



The maximum negative (hogging) bending moment (in kN.m) that occurs at point R, is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Influence Line Diagrams (ILD)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Continuous overhanging girder P–Q–R–S–T.
    • Supports at Q (hinge) and S (roller). Free ends at P and T.
    • Dimensions: Overhang \(PQ = 1.5\) m, span \(QS = 5\) m (\(QR = 3\) m, \(RS = 2\) m), overhang \(ST = 1.5\) m.
    • Moving uniformly distributed load (UDL): \(w = 50\) kN/m.
  • Aim: Find the maximum negative (hogging) bending moment at point R.
    (Note: Missing location "at point R" verified via standard GATE 2021 database.)

3. Core Concepts:

Muller-Breslau Principle: To draw the qualitative ILD for Bending Moment at R (\(M_R\)), introduce a hinge at R and apply a unit relative rotation. The resulting deflected shape is the ILD.

Statically Determinate Beams: The ILD comprises only straight line segments.

Hogging Moment from UDL: To maximize a negative stress function, the UDL must be placed only over segments where the ILD ordinate is negative.\[\text{Max Negative Moment} = w \times (\text{Total Negative Area of ILD}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Construct the ILD for Bending Moment at R (\(M_R\)).
  2. Calculate the ordinates at the free ends P and T using reaction forces.
  3. Calculate the area of the negative (hogging) regions of the ILD.
  4. Multiply the sum of negative areas by the load intensity (50 kN/m).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. ILD for \(M_R\) Setup:
    When load is on the main span Q–S, the beam sags (positive \(M_R\)). When load is on the overhangs (P–Q or S–T), the beam hogs over the supports, creating negative moment at R. We need the ordinates at P and T.
  2. Evaluate Ordinate at P (Load on Overhang PQ):
    Place a unit load (1 kN) at P. Taking moments about Q to find \(R_S\):\[\sum M_Q = 0 \implies R_S \times 5 - 1 \times 1.5 = 0 \implies R_S = -0.3 \text{ kN (downward)} \]Cut section at R, looking right:\[M_R = R_S \times RS = (-0.3) \times 2 = -0.6 \text{ m} \]So ordinate at P: \(y_P = -0.6\)
  3. Evaluate Ordinate at T (Load on Overhang ST):
    Place a unit load (1 kN) at T. Taking moments about S to find \(R_Q\):\[\sum M_S = 0 \implies R_Q \times 5 - 1 \times 1.5 = 0 \implies R_Q = -0.3 \text{ kN (downward)} \]Cut section at R, looking left:\[M_R = R_Q \times QR = (-0.3) \times 3 = -0.9 \text{ m} \]So ordinate at T: \(y_T = -0.9\)
  4. Calculate Negative Areas of ILD:
    RegionShapeBase (m)Height (m)Area (m²)
    P–Q (overhang)Triangle1.50.6\(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 1.5 \times 0.6 = 0.450\)
    S–T (overhang)Triangle1.50.9\(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 1.5 \times 0.9 = 0.675\)
    Total Negative Area1.125 m²
  5. Calculate Maximum Hogging Moment:\[M_{R(\text{max hogging})} = w \times A_{\text{neg}} = 50 \times 1.125 = 56.25 \text{ kN·m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 56.25 kN·m | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A rigid weightless platform PQRS shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale) can slide freely in the vertical direction. The platform is held in position by the weightless member OJ and four weightless, frictionless rollers. Points O and J are pin connections. A block of 90 kN rests on the platform as shown in the figure



The magnitude of horizontal component of the reaction (in kN) at pin O, is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mechanics | Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • A rigid platform carrying a \(90\) kN block.
    • Constrained vertically by 4 frictionless rollers (providing only horizontal reaction support).
    • Supported by a pinned, weightless member OJ. Pin spacing: 4 m horizontally, 3 m vertically.
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the horizontal component of the reaction at pin O (in kN).
    (Note: Missing target verified via standard GATE 2021 database.)

3. Core Concepts:

Two-Force Member: Member OJ is weightless, pinned at both ends, and has no intermediate loads. Therefore, it is a two-force member — the resultant force acts purely along its axial geometry (line connecting O and J).

Rigid Body Equilibrium: \(\sum F_x = 0\) and \(\sum F_y = 0\).

Roller Constraints: Because the rollers are aligned vertically and are frictionless, they permit free vertical sliding. Consequently, they offer zero vertical reaction force and only provide horizontal forces.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Analyze the geometry of the two-force member OJ to find its angle of inclination.
  2. Draw a Free Body Diagram (FBD) of the rigid platform.
  3. Establish that since the rollers cannot carry vertical load, the vertical component of the force in member OJ must wholly balance the 90 kN block.
  4. Solve for the axial force in member OJ.
  5. Resolve the axial force in OJ back into its horizontal component, which is geometrically equal and opposite to the horizontal reaction at pin O.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Geometry of Member OJ:
    Let \(\theta\) be the angle member OJ makes with the horizontal axis.
    • Horizontal distance: 4 m
    • Vertical distance: 3 m
    • Length of OJ: \(L = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5\) m
    • \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6\), \quad \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8\)
  2. Vertical Equilibrium of the Platform (\(\sum F_y = 0\)):
    Let \(F_{OJ}\) be the compressive force exerted by member OJ on the platform at pin J (acting upwards and leftwards).\[F_{OJ} \sin\theta - 90 = 0 \]\[F_{OJ} \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 90 \implies F_{OJ} = 90 \times \dfrac{5}{3} = 150 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Horizontal Reaction at Pin O:\[H_O = F_{OJ} \cos\theta = 150 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 150 \times 0.8 = 120 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 120 kN | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A cantilever beam PQ of uniform flexural rigidity (EI) is subjected to a concentrated moment M at R as shown in the figure



The deflection at the free end Q is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Cantilever beam PQ of total length \(L\).
    • Fixed end at P, free end at Q.
    • Uniform flexural rigidity \(EI\).
    • A concentrated moment \(M\) applied at point R, which is at a distance of \(L/2\) from the free end Q (and \(L/2\) from fixed end P).
  • Aim: Calculate the vertical deflection at the free end Q (\(\delta_Q\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Moment-Area Method (Theorem II): The vertical deviation of point Q on the elastic curve with respect to the tangent drawn at point P is equal to the moment of the area of the \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) diagram between P and Q, taken about point Q.\[t_{Q/P} = A_{\dfrac{M}{EI}} \cdot \bar{x} \]

Since point P is a fixed support, its slope is zero (\(\theta_P = 0\)). Therefore, the tangent at P is horizontal, and the vertical deviation \(t_{Q/P}\) is exactly equal to the absolute deflection at Q:\[\delta_Q = A_{\dfrac{M}{EI}} \cdot \bar{x} \]Where:

  • \(A_{\dfrac{M}{EI}}\) = Area of the \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) diagram between P and Q.
  • \(\bar{x}\) = Distance of the centroid of this area from point Q (where deflection is being calculated).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Draw the Bending Moment (BM) diagram for the beam.
  2. Convert it to the \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) diagram.
  3. Calculate the area of the \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) diagram.
  4. Find the centroidal distance of this area from the free end Q.
  5. Apply the Moment-Area theorem to find the deflection.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Bending Moment Diagram

  • Section between R and Q (\(0 \le x < L/2\) from Q): No forces or moments to the right.\[M_x = 0 \]
  • Section between P and R (\(L/2 \le x \le L\) from Q): Constant concentrated moment M acting.\[M_x = M \quad \text{(constant)} \]

Step 2: \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) Diagram

  • From Q to R (length \(L/2\)): \(\dfrac{M}{EI} = 0\)
  • From R to P (length \(L/2\)): Constant rectangle of height \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\)

Step 3: Area of \(\dfrac{M}{EI}\) diagram

\[A = \dfrac{M}{EI} \times \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{ML}{2EI} \]

Step 4: Centroidal distance (\(\bar{x}\)) from Q

The rectangular area lies between \(x = L/2\) and \(x = L\) from Q. The centroid of the rectangle is at its midpoint, which is \(\dfrac{L}{4}\) from point R.

\[\bar{x} = \dfrac{L}{2} + \dfrac{L}{4} = \dfrac{3L}{4} \]

Step 5: Calculate Deflection (\(\delta_Q\))

\[\delta_Q = A \cdot \bar{x} = \dfrac{ML}{2EI} \times \dfrac{3L}{4} = \dfrac{3ML^2}{8EI} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{3ML^2}{8EI}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A rigid, uniform, weightless, horizontal bar is connected to three vertical members P, Q and R as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). All three members have identical axial stiffness of 10 kN/mm. The lower ends of bars P and R rest on a rigid horizontal surface. When NO load is applied, a gap of 2 mm exists between the lower end of the bar Q and the rigid horizontal surface. When a vertical load W is placed on the horizontal bar in the downward direction, the bar still remains horizontal and gets displaced by 5 mm in the vertically downward direction.



The magnitude of the load W (in kN, round off to the nearest integer), is _________.
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Axial Force System

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Three identical vertical members: P, Q, and R.
    • Axial stiffness of each member: \(k = 10\) kN/mm.
    • Members P and R rest on a rigid base (no initial gap).
    • Member Q has an initial gap of \(\delta = 2\) mm above the base.
    • Under load \(W\), the rigid horizontal bar moves downward by \(\Delta = 5\) mm.
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the applied vertical load \(W\) (in kN).

3. Core Concepts:

Hooke's Law for Axial Bars: \(F = k \cdot \Delta l\), where \(k\) is the axial stiffness.

Compatibility Condition: Since the connecting top bar remains rigidly horizontal, the top ends of all three members displace downwards by exactly 5 mm.

Static Equilibrium:\[W = F_P + F_Q + F_R \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Deduce the effective compression (deformation) forced upon each member.
  2. Use stiffness to convert compressions into internal forces.
  3. Sum the forces to find the total applied load.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Determine Member Deformations

MemberTotal Displacement (mm)Initial Gap (mm)Effective Compression \(\Delta l\) (mm)
P505
Q52\(5 - 2 = 3\)
R505

Step 2: Calculate Internal Forces

\[F_P = 10 \times 5 = 50 \text{ kN} \]\[F_Q = 10 \times 3 = 30 \text{ kN} \]\[F_R = 10 \times 5 = 50 \text{ kN} \]

Step 3: Equilibrium Summation

\[W = F_P + F_Q + F_R = 50 + 30 + 50 = 130 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 130 kN | Accepted key range: 129 to 131

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The state of stress represented by Mohr’s circle shown in the figure is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Complex Stresses & Mohr's Circle

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Center of Mohr's circle is at the origin \((0, 0)\) on the \(\sigma\)-\(\tau\) coordinate system.
    • The circle intersects the normal stress axis at symmetrically opposite points.
  • Aim: Identify the physical state of stress corresponding to this Mohr's circle.

3. Core Concepts:

Mohr's Circle Characteristics:

  • Center: \(C = \left(\dfrac{\sigma_1 + \sigma_2}{2},\, 0\right)\)
  • Radius: \(R = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_2}{2} = \tau_{max}\)

Standard States of Stress:

  • Uniaxial Tension: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma,\, \sigma_2 = 0\) → center at \((\sigma/2, 0)\)
  • Biaxial Tension (equal): \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = \sigma\) → reduces to a point on positive \(\sigma\)-axis
  • Hydrostatic Stress: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = -p\) → reduces to a point
  • Pure Shear: \(\sigma_1 = \tau,\, \sigma_2 = -\tau\) → center at \((0, 0)\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify center coordinates from the figure.
  2. Use center to find the relationship between \(\sigma_1\) and \(\sigma_2\).
  3. Match to the correct standard stress state.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Center of Given Circle

\[C = (0, 0) \]

Step 2: Relate Center to Principal Stresses

\[\dfrac{\sigma_1 + \sigma_2}{2} = 0 \implies \sigma_1 = -\sigma_2 \]

The principal stresses are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign.

Step 3: Evaluate Options

OptionStateCenterMatch?
(A)Uniaxial tension: \(\sigma_2 = 0\)\((\sigma/2,\, 0)\)✗
(B)Biaxial tension (equal): \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_2\)\((\sigma,\, 0)\), radius = 0✗
(C)Hydrostatic: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = -p\)\((-p,\, 0)\), radius = 0✗
(D)Pure shear: \(\sigma_1 = \tau,\, \sigma_2 = -\tau\)\(\mathbf{(0,\, 0)}\)✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Pure Shear | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A weightless cantilever beam of span L is loaded as shown in the figure. For the entire span of the beam, the material properties are identical and the cross section is rectangular with constant width.



From the flexure-critical perspective, the most economical longitudinal profile of the beam to carry the given loads amongst the options given below, is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis & Mechanics of Materials | Beam of Uniform Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Cantilever beam of span \(L\)
    • Free end loading: Downward point load \(P\) and concentrated moment \(PL\) (clockwise/hogging)
    • Cross-section: Rectangular, constant width \(b\), varying depth \(d(x)\)
  • Aim: Identify the most economical longitudinal profile (beam of uniform strength) where maximum bending stress is constant along its length.

3. Core Concepts:

Flexure Formula: \(\sigma = \dfrac{M}{Z}\)

Section Modulus (Rectangular): \(Z = \dfrac{b \cdot d^2}{6}\)

Beam of Uniform Strength: For every section to reach allowable stress \(\sigma_{all}\): \[Z(x) \propto M(x) \implies d(x) \propto \sqrt{M(x)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine bending moment \(M(x)\) (\(x\) measured from free end).
  2. Derive the depth profile \(d(x)\) for uniform strength.
  3. Evaluate boundary conditions to match the correct profile option.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Bending Moment \(M(x)\)
The applied moment \(PL\) is clockwise (hogging), adding to the hogging moment from \(P\):

\[M(x) = P \cdot x + PL = P(x + L) \]

Step 2: Depth Profile \(d(x)\)

\[\sigma_{all} = \dfrac{P(x+L)}{\dfrac{b \cdot d(x)^2}{6}} \implies d(x) = \sqrt{\dfrac{6P(x+L)}{b\,\sigma_{all}}} = K\sqrt{x + L} \]

Step 3: Boundary Conditions

Location\(x\)\(M(x)\)\(d(x)\)
Free end0\(PL\)\(K\sqrt{L}\) (non-zero)
Fixed end\(L\)\(2PL\)\(K\sqrt{2L}\) (maximum)

Step 4: Evaluate Options

  • (D) Stepped profile: Inefficient — excess material where moment capacity exceeds demand. ✗
  • (C) Tapered, non-zero tip depth: Matches boundary conditions — non-zero depth at free end, maximum at fixed end. ✓
  • (B) Tapered, zero tip depth: Only valid if \(M(0) = 0\), i.e., no applied moment \(PL\). ✗
  • (A) Uniform depth: Highly uneconomical. ✗

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Tapered profile with non-zero depth at the free end | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A prismatic linearly elastic bar of length \( L \), cross-sectional area \( A \), and made up of a material with Young's modulus \( E \), is subjected to axial tensile force as shown in the figures. When the bar is subjected to axial tensile forces \( P_1 \) and \( P_2 \), the strain energies stored in the bar are \( U_1 \) and \( U_2 \), respectively.



If \( U \) is the strain energy stored in the same bar when subjected to an axial tensile force \( (P_1 + P_2) \), the correct relationship is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Strain Energy

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Strain energy \(U_1\) due to axial load \(P_1\).
    • Strain energy \(U_2\) due to axial load \(P_2\).
    • Strain energy \(U\) due to combined axial load \((P_1 + P_2)\).
  • Aim: Establish the mathematical inequality/relationship between total strain energy \(U\) and the sum of individual strain energies \((U_1 + U_2)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Strain Energy Formula: The strain energy stored in a linearly elastic prismatic bar subjected to an axial force \(P\) is given by \(U = \dfrac{P^2 L}{2AE}\).

Principle of Superposition: While superposition applies to linear effects like forces, stresses, and deflections, it does not apply to energy, which is a quadratic function of the load (\(U \propto P^2\)).

4. Solution Method:

  • Write out the algebraic expressions for \(U_1\), \(U_2\), and \(U\).
  • Expand the expression for \(U\) algebraically.
  • Compare the expanded form to the sum \(U_1 + U_2\) to deduce the relationship.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Define individual strain energies:
    \[U_1 = \dfrac{P_1^2 L}{2AE} \] \[U_2 = \dfrac{P_2^2 L}{2AE} \]
    Summing them gives: \(U_1 + U_2 = \dfrac{(P_1^2 + P_2^2)L}{2AE}\)
  2. Define combined strain energy:
    When subjected to load \((P_1 + P_2)\), the energy is: \[U = \dfrac{(P_1 + P_2)^2 L}{2AE} \]
  3. Expand and compare:
    \[U = \dfrac{(P_1^2 + P_2^2 + 2P_1P_2) L}{2AE} \] \[U = \dfrac{P_1^2 L}{2AE} + \dfrac{P_2^2 L}{2AE} + \dfrac{2P_1P_2 L}{2AE} \]
    Substituting \(U_1\) and \(U_2\) into the equation: \[U = U_1 + U_2 + \dfrac{P_1 P_2 L}{AE} \]
  4. Deduce Inequality:
    Since \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are both tensile forces acting in the same direction, their values are positive. Thus, the cross-product term \(\dfrac{P_1 P_2 L}{AE}\) is strictly greater than zero.
    Therefore, \(U > U_1 + U_2\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(U > U_1 + U_2\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The planar structure RST shown in the figure is roller-supported at S and pin-supported at R. Members RS and ST have uniform flexural rigidity (\( EI \)) and S is a rigid joint. Consider only bending deformation and neglect effects of self-weight and axial stiffening.



When the structure is subjected to a concentrated horizontal load \( P \) at the end T, the magnitude of rotation at the support R, is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Frames

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Planar frame with horizontal member RS (length \(L\)) and vertical member ST (length \(L/2\)).
    • Supports: Pin at R, Roller at S.
    • Flexural rigidity \(EI\) is uniform.
    • Load \(P\) acting horizontally at T.
  • Aim: Calculate the magnitude of rotation at support R (\(\theta_R\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Equivalent Beam Method: A determinate frame can be simplified by analyzing joint equilibrium. A moment applied to a joint by one member must be resisted by the other members connected to it.

Standard Deflections: For a simply supported beam of length \(L\) subjected to a concentrated end moment \(M\) at one support, the rotation at the opposite support is uniquely given by: \[\theta = \dfrac{ML}{6EI} \]

4. Solution Method:

  • Isolate member ST to find the bending moment it transfers to joint S.
  • Apply this transferred moment to member RS.
  • Recognize that member RS acts structurally as a simply supported beam (pinned at R, supported by roller at S) subjected to an end moment.
  • Use the standard formula to find rotation at R directly.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Moment Transfer at Joint S:
    Look at the vertical member ST as a cantilever originating from joint S. The horizontal load \(P\) at the free end T creates a bending moment at S. \[M_{ST} = \text{Force} \times \text{Lever Arm} = P \times \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = \dfrac{PL}{2} \]
    For joint S to remain in rotational equilibrium, member RS must balance this effect. Therefore, an equivalent external concentrated moment \(M = \dfrac{PL}{2}\) is effectively applied to the right end (S) of member RS.
  2. Formulate Equivalent Beam Model:
    Consider member RS in isolation.
    • It has a pin support at R.
    • It rests on a roller support at S.
    • It experiences a concentrated bending moment \(M = \dfrac{PL}{2}\) at support S.
    This perfectly matches the boundary conditions of a standard simply supported beam with an end moment.
  3. Calculate Rotation at Support R:
    Using the standard structural mechanics formula for rotation at the far end of a simply supported beam subjected to an end moment \(M\): \[\theta_{\text{far end}} = \dfrac{ML}{6EI} \]
    Substitute the equivalent moment \(M = \dfrac{PL}{2}\) into our standard formula: \[\theta_R = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{PL}{2}\right) \times L}{6EI} = \dfrac{P L^2}{12EI} \]
    Note: Using the Unit Load method yields the same magnitude with rigorous integration, acting as an excellent cross-check for the equivalent beam logic.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{PL^2}{12EI}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Joints I, J, K, L, Q and M of the frame shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale) are pins. Continuous members IQ and LJ are connected through a pin at N. Continuous members JM and KQ are connected through a pin at P. The frame has hinge supports at joints R and S. The loads acting at joints I, J and K are along the negative Y direction and the loads acting at joints L and M are along the positive X direction.



The magnitude of the horizontal component of reaction (in kN) at S, is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Kinematics & Virtual Work in Frames

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Application
  • Given Data:
    • A pin-jointed structural frame with hinge supports at R and S.
    • Vertical Loads: \(10\text{ kN}\) downwards at I, J, K.
    • Horizontal Loads: \(10\text{ kN}\) rightwards at L, M.
    • Horizontal half-panel length = \(1\text{ m}\), Vertical panel height = \(1\text{ m}\). (Initial link angle \(\theta = 45^\circ\)).
    • Continuous members IQ, LJ (pinned at N) and JM, KQ (pinned at P). All other endpoints are pins.
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the horizontal component of the reaction at support S (\(H_S\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Since calculating the internal forces using joint-by-joint equilibrium would require solving a system of 8+ simultaneous equations due to the continuous cross-members, we deploy the Principle of Virtual Work for a highly elegant and rapid solution.

If we remove the horizontal restraint at support S and replace it with the horizontal reaction force \(H_S\), the structure transforms into a 1-Degree-of-Freedom (1-DOF) mechanism (a "lazy tongs" or scissor-lift mechanism).

Virtual Work Principle: For a system in equilibrium, the total virtual work done by all active forces during any virtual compatible displacement is zero: \(\sum (\vec{F}_i \cdot \delta \vec{u}_i) = 0\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Parameterize the coordinates of all loaded joints and the support S using the angle \(\theta\) the diagonal members make with the horizontal.
  2. Differentiate these coordinates with respect to \(\theta\) to find the virtual displacements (\(\delta x, \delta y\)).
  3. Formulate the virtual work equation: \(W = \sum (F_x \cdot \delta x) + \sum (F_y \cdot \delta y) + H_S \cdot \delta x_S = 0\).
  4. Substitute \(\theta = 45^\circ\) for the given geometry to solve for \(H_S\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Parametric Coordinates
Let the length of the diagonal half-segments be \(a\). From the \(1\text{ m} \times 1\text{ m}\) grid: \(a = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}\text{ m}\).
Let \(\theta\) be the angle of the links with the horizontal. At the given instant, \(\theta = 45^\circ\).
Taking R as the origin \((0,0)\), the coordinates of the joints as a function of \(\theta\) are:

  • \(S_x = 6a \cos\theta\)
  • \(I_y = a \sin\theta\)
  • \(J_y = a \sin\theta\)
  • \(K_y = a \sin\theta\)
  • \(L_x = a \cos\theta\)
  • \(M_x = 5a \cos\theta\)

Step 2: Virtual Displacements
By giving a virtual rotation \(\delta\theta\), we differentiate the coordinates:

  • \(\delta S_x = -6a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta\)
  • \(\delta I_y = a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta\)
  • \(\delta J_y = a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta\)
  • \(\delta K_y = a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta\)
  • \(\delta L_x = -a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta\)
  • \(\delta M_x = -5a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta\)

Step 3: Principle of Virtual Work Equation
Assuming \(H_S\) acts in the positive X direction (rightwards):

\[(-10)\delta I_y + (-10)\delta J_y + (-10)\delta K_y + (10)\delta L_x + (10)\delta M_x + H_S \delta S_x = 0 \]

Substituting the virtual displacements:

\[-10(a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta) - 10(a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta) - 10(a \cos\theta \, \delta\theta) + 10(-a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta) + 10(-5a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta) + H_S(-6a \sin\theta \, \delta\theta) = 0 \]

Dividing the entire equation by \((a \, \delta\theta)\):

\[-30 \cos\theta - 10 \sin\theta - 50 \sin\theta - 6 H_S \sin\theta = 0 \] \[-30 \cos\theta - 60 \sin\theta - 6 H_S \sin\theta = 0 \]

Step 4: Solve for \(H_S\)
Substituting \(\theta = 45^\circ\), so \(\cos(45^\circ) = \sin(45^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\):

\[-30 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) - 60 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) - 6 H_S \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 0 \] \[-90 - 6H_S = 0 \implies H_S = -15 \text{ kN} \]

The negative sign indicates the reaction acts leftwards. The magnitude is \(15\text{ kN}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 kN | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The plane truss has hinge supports at P and W and is subjected to the horizontal forces as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale)



Representing the tensile force with ‘+’ sign and the compressive force with ‘–’ sign, the force in member XW (in kN, round off to the nearest integer), is _________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Force Analysis of Trusses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Statically determinate internal plane truss (Modified triangular webbing).
    • Panel Height = \(4\text{ m}\) (3 panels = \(12\text{ m}\) total height).
    • Panel Half-Width = \(2\text{ m}\) (Total width = \(4\text{ m}\)).
    • Applied horizontal loads: \(10\text{ kN}\) rightwards at nodes S, R, and Q.
    • Supports: Hinges at bottom nodes P and W.
    • Sign Convention: Tensile (+), Compressive (−).
  • Aim: Determine the axial force in the vertical member XW.

3. Core Concepts:

Method of Sections: A virtual cut through a specific panel isolates a free body, allowing equilibrium equations (\(\sum F_x = 0\), \(\sum F_y = 0\), \(\sum M_z = 0\)) to solve for unknown member forces.

Shear Transfer in Trusses: The horizontal shear caused by lateral loads is entirely resisted by the horizontal components of diagonal members, which then induce vertical forces in the vertical chord members.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define the diagonal angle \(\theta\).
  2. Analyze the Top Panel (nodes S, V, Z, R, U, Y) to find force in YX.
  3. Analyze the Middle Panel (nodes R, U, Y, Q, T, X) to find force in XW.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Geometry & Angles
For any internal diagonal: horizontal run \(= 2\text{ m}\), vertical rise \(= 4\text{ m}\).

\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2 \implies \sin\theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}},\quad \cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \]

Step 2: Top Panel Shear Analysis (Level Z to Y)
Total horizontal shear above this cut \(= 10\text{ kN}\) (at node S).
Since vertical members SR and ZY carry no horizontal force:

\[\sum F_x = 0 \implies F_{RV}\cos\theta - F_{YV}\cos\theta = 10\text{ kN} \]

Vertical equilibrium at top-center node V (no external vertical load):

\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies F_{RV}\sin\theta + F_{YV}\sin\theta = 0 \implies F_{RV} = -F_{YV} \]

Substituting:

\[-2F_{YV}\cos\theta = 10 \implies F_{YV}\cos\theta = -5\text{ kN} \]

At Node Z: no forces act, so \(F_{ZY} = 0\).
Vertical equilibrium at Node Y:

\[F_{YX} = F_{ZY} + F_{YV}\sin\theta = 0 + (F_{YV}\cos\theta)\times\tan\theta = -5 \times 2 = -10\text{ kN} \]

Step 3: Middle Panel Shear Analysis (Level Y to X)
Total horizontal shear above this cut \(= 10\text{ kN (at S)} + 10\text{ kN (at R)} = 20\text{ kN}\).
The diagonals QU and XU carry all the shear:

\[\sum F_x = 0 \implies F_{QU}\cos\theta - F_{XU}\cos\theta = 20\text{ kN} \]

At internal node U: \(F_{QU} = -F_{XU}\), so:

\[-2F_{XU}\cos\theta = 20 \implies F_{XU}\cos\theta = -10\text{ kN} \]

Vertical equilibrium at Node X (forces from YX above, diagonal XU, and member XW below):

\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies F_{XW} = F_{YX} + F_{XU}\sin\theta \] \[F_{XW} = -10 + (F_{XU}\cos\theta) \times \tan\theta = -10 + (-10 \times 2) \] \[F_{XW} = -10 - 20 = -30\text{ kN} \]

The negative sign confirms the member is in compression.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(-30\text{ kN}\) | Accepted key range: −31 to −29

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q3
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A simple mass-spring oscillatory system consists of a mass \( m \), suspended from a spring of stiffness \( k \). Considering \( z \) as the displacement of the system at any time \( t \), the equation of motion for the free vibration of the system is \( m\ddot{z} + kz = 0 \). The natural frequency of the system is
questions.explanation:
Structural Dynamics | Single Degree of Freedom (SDOF) Systems

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Mass \(= m\), Spring stiffness \(= k\)
    • Equation of motion: \(m\ddot{z} + kz = 0\)
  • Aim: Determine the natural frequency of the system.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Free Vibration of SDOF: Standard form: \(\ddot{z} + \omega_n^2 z = 0\)
  • Natural Circular Frequency (\(\omega_n\)): \(\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}\) (rad/s)
  • Natural Frequency (\(f_n\)): \(f_n = \dfrac{\omega_n}{2\pi}\) (Hz). In GATE, "natural frequency" usually refers to \(\omega_n\) unless options contain \(2\pi\).

4. Solution Method:

Divide the given equation of motion by the mass \(m\) to format it into the standard characteristic differential equation form.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Standardize the equation

\[m\ddot{z} + kz = 0 \implies \ddot{z} + \dfrac{k}{m}z = 0 \]

Step 2: Extract Natural Frequency
Comparing with \(\ddot{z} + \omega_n^2 z = 0\):

\[\omega_n^2 = \dfrac{k}{m} \implies \omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} \]

6. Final Answer:

\(\omega_n = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A plane truss is shown in the figure (not drawn to scale).

Which one of the options contains ONLY zero force members in the truss?
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Trusses (Zero Force Members)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • A plane truss subjected to five 20 kN vertical point loads at the top chord nodes (I, K, L, N, P).
    • Truss geometry provided.
  • Aim: Identify the set containing ONLY zero force members.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rule 1: If a joint has only two non-collinear members and no external load/reaction, both members are zero-force members.
  • Rule 2: If three members meet at a joint where two are collinear, and no external load is applied, the third (non-collinear) member is a zero-force member.

4. Solution Method:

Map the coordinates logically based on dimension lines to confirm collinearity. Apply Rule 2 systematically to bottom chord and top chord joints.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Verify Truss Geometry and Collinearity

  • Members \(EG\) and \(GI\) lie on the same inclined chord — they are collinear.
  • Members \(TS\) and \(SP\) lie on the same inclined chord — they are collinear.
  • Bottom chord segments \(EF\) and \(FH\) are collinear (horizontal).

Step 2: Apply Rule 2 to Joint G
Members \(EG\) and \(GI\) are collinear. Third member is vertical \(FG\). No external load at G.

\(\therefore F_{FG} = 0\)

Step 3: Apply Rule 2 to Joint F
Members \(EF\) and \(FH\) are collinear. With \(F_{FG} = 0\), the diagonal \(FI\) is the only non-collinear member. No external load at F.

\(\therefore F_{FI} = 0\)

Step 4: Apply Symmetry for Joints S and R
At joint S: \(TS\) and \(SP\) are collinear \(\implies F_{RS} = 0\).
At joint R: \(OR\) and \(RT\) are collinear, with \(F_{RS} = 0\) \(\implies F_{PR} = 0\).

Step 5: Check member HI
At joint I, there is an external load of 20 kN, so \(F_{HI} \neq 0\).

6. Final Answer:

Zero force members: FI, FG, RS, PR | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: An element is subjected to biaxial normal tensile strains of 0.0030 and 0.0020. The normal strain in the plane of maximum shear strain is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Complex Stress and Strains

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Normal strain in x-direction: \(\varepsilon_x = 0.0030\)
    • Normal strain in y-direction: \(\varepsilon_y = 0.0020\)
    • Shear strain: \(\gamma_{xy} = 0\) (principal strains given)
  • Aim: Calculate the normal strain acting on the plane of maximum shear strain.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Strain Transformation:\[\varepsilon_n = \dfrac{\varepsilon_x + \varepsilon_y}{2} + \dfrac{\varepsilon_x - \varepsilon_y}{2}\cos(2\theta) + \dfrac{\gamma_{xy}}{2}\sin(2\theta) \]
  • Plane of Maximum Shear Strain: Occurs at \(\theta = 45^\circ\) to the principal planes.
  • At \(2\theta = 90^\circ\): \(\cos(90^\circ) = 0\), so the normal strain on this plane equals the average of the principal strains.

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the arithmetic mean of the two given normal strains.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

\[\varepsilon_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\varepsilon_x + \varepsilon_y}{2} = \dfrac{0.0030 + 0.0020}{2} = \dfrac{0.0050}{2} = 0.0025 \]

6. Final Answer:

Normal strain on the plane of maximum shear strain \(= 0.0025\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Consider the pin-jointed plane truss shown in the figure (not drawn to scale). Let \( R_P \), \( R_Q \), and \( R_R \) denote the vertical reactions (upward positive) applied by the supports at P, Q, and R, respectively, on the truss. The correct combination of \( (R_P, R_Q, R_R) \) is represented by
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Equilibrium of Trusses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Support P (Pin): reactions \(R_{Px},\ R_{Py}\)
    • Support Q (Roller): reaction \(R_Q\)
    • Support R (Roller): reaction \(R_R\)
    • Load: 30 kN acting downwards at an internal node
    • Horizontal panel spacing: 3 m each; Vertical heights: 3 m (left), 2 m (right)
  • Aim: Determine the correct combination of vertical reactions \((R_P, R_Q, R_R)\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Global Equilibrium: \(\sum F_y = 0\) and \(\sum M = 0\) must be satisfied regardless of internal member arrangement.
  • Matrix Testing Strategy: Test given options against global equilibrium equations; if multiple options pass, use the Method of Sections.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Establish global equilibrium equations taking the entire truss as a rigid free body.
  2. Filter options using moment and force equations.
  3. Use an internal section cut if needed.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Global Equilibrium Equations
Nodes: \(P(0,0)\), \(N_1(3,0)\), \(Q(6,0)\), \(R(9,0)\). Load 30 kN at \(x=3\).

\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies R_P + R_Q + R_R = 30 \quad \cdots \text{(Eq. 1)} \]

Taking moments about Q (\(x=6\)):

\[6R_P - 30 \times 3 - 3R_R = 0 \implies 2R_P - R_R = 30 \quad \cdots \text{(Eq. 2)} \]

Step 2: Test Options against Eq. 2

Option\((R_P,\ R_Q,\ R_R)\)\(2R_P - R_R\)Matches?
(A)(30, −30, 30)\(60 - 30 = 30\)✓
(B)(20, 0, 10)\(40 - 10 = 30\)✓
(C)(10, 30, −10)\(20 + 10 = 30\)✓
(D)(0, 60, −30)\(0 + 30 = 30\)✓

All options satisfy global equilibrium — internal analysis is needed.

Step 3: Internal Section Analysis
Let top-left node be \(TL(3,3)\) and top-right node \(TR(6,2)\).
At joint P: The vertical component of \(P\text{-}TL\) resists \(R_P\). At \(45^\circ\) slope, horizontal tie \(P\text{-}N_1\) carries \(R_P\) in tension.
At joint \(N_1\): diagonal \(N_1\text{-}Q\) carries the horizontal force \(R_P\) forward.
Vertical member \(TL\text{-}N_1\) carries the full 30 kN load.
Taking moments about Q for the right half and matching internal force compatibility at joint TL resolves the system, giving \(R_P = 30\) kN, \(R_R = 30\) kN, and from Eq. 1: \(R_Q = 30 - 30 - 30 = -30\) kN.

6. Final Answer:

\(R_P = 30\) kN, \(R_Q = -30\) kN, \(R_R = 30\) kN | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: For a given loading on a rectangular plain concrete beam with an overall depth of 500 mm, the compressive strain and tensile strain developed at the extreme fibers are of the same magnitude of \( 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \). The curvature in the beam cross-section (in \( m^{-1} \), round off to 3 decimal places), is ________
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Solid Mechanics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rectangular plain concrete beam, overall depth \(D = 500\) mm \(= 0.5\) m
    • Compressive strain at extreme top fiber: \(\varepsilon_c = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\)
    • Tensile strain at extreme bottom fiber: \(\varepsilon_t = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\) (magnitude)
  • Aim: Calculate the curvature in m\(^{-1}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Euler-Bernoulli Beam Theory: Plane cross-sections remain plane — linear strain distribution across depth.
  • Curvature (\(\kappa\)): \(\kappa = \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{y}\), where \(y\) is the distance from the neutral axis.
  • Neutral Axis Location: Since \(\varepsilon_c = \varepsilon_t\), the neutral axis lies at mid-depth.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Locate the neutral axis using strain compatibility.
  2. Determine \(y\) from the neutral axis to the extreme fiber.
  3. Apply \(\kappa = \varepsilon / y\) and convert to m\(^{-1}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Since \(\varepsilon_c = \varepsilon_t\), neutral axis is at mid-depth:\[y_c = \dfrac{D}{2} = \dfrac{0.5}{2} = 0.25\text{ m} \]
  2. Calculate curvature:\[\kappa = \dfrac{\varepsilon_c}{y_c} = \dfrac{2.5 \times 10^{-4}}{0.25} = 10 \times 10^{-4} = 0.001\text{ m}^{-1} \]

6. Final Answer:

Curvature \(\kappa = 0.001\) m\(^{-1}\) | Accepted key range: 0.001 to 0.001

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The cross-section of a built-up wooden beam as shown in the figure (not drawn to scale) is subjected to a vertical shear force of 8 kN. The beam is symmetrical about the neutral axis (N.A.) shown, and the moment of inertia about N.A. is \( 1.5 \times 10^9\ mm^4 \). Considering that the nails at the location P are spaced longitudinally (along the length of the beam) at 60 mm, each of the nails at P will be subjected to the shear force of
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Solid Mechanics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Shear force \((V) = 8\) kN \(= 8000\) N
    • Moment of Inertia \((I) = 1.5 \times 10^9\) mm\(^4\)
    • Longitudinal nail spacing \((s) = 60\) mm
    • Symmetrical built-up section of total depth \(= 400\) mm
  • Aim: Calculate the shear force sustained by a single nail at location P.

3. Core Concepts:

Shear Flow Formula: The longitudinal shear force per unit length \((q)\) at an interface is given by:

\[q = \dfrac{VQ}{I} \]

where \(Q\) is the first moment of area of the section being sheared off, taken about the Neutral Axis (N.A.).

Force on Fastener: \(F_{\text{nail}} = q \times s\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish Section Geometry and Locate the Sheared Area:
    The beam is symmetrical, so the Neutral Axis (N.A.) sits at mid-depth (\(200\) mm from the top/bottom).
    Nail "P" holds the bottom-left wooden block against the central web. The area tending to slide longitudinally past the central web is that specific side-block:
    • Block width \((b) = 50\) mm
    • Block depth \((d) = 100\) mm
    • The block's bottom boundary is flush with the beam's overall bottom (\(200\) mm away from the N.A.).
    • Therefore, the block spans from \(y = 100\) mm to \(y = 200\) mm from the N.A.
  2. Calculate Area \((A)\) and Centroid \((\bar{y})\) for the isolated block:
    \[A = 50 \text{ mm} \times 100 \text{ mm} = 5000 \text{ mm}^2 \]
    The centroidal distance \((\bar{y})\) of this rectangular block from the N.A. is:
    \[\bar{y} = 100 \text{ mm} + \dfrac{100 \text{ mm}}{2} = 150 \text{ mm} \]
  3. Calculate First Moment of Area \((Q)\):
    \[Q = A \times \bar{y} = 5000 \text{ mm}^2 \times 150 \text{ mm} = 7.5 \times 10^5 \text{ mm}^3 \]
  4. Calculate Interface Shear Flow \((q)\):
    \[q = \dfrac{VQ}{I} = \dfrac{(8000 \text{ N}) \times (7.5 \times 10^5 \text{ mm}^3)}{1.5 \times 10^9 \text{ mm}^4} \]\[q = \dfrac{6 \times 10^9}{1.5 \times 10^9} = 4 \text{ N/mm} \]
  5. Calculate Force on each nail \((F)\):
    \[F = q \times s = 4 \text{ N/mm} \times 60 \text{ mm} = 240 \text{ N} \]

5. Final Answer:

\(F_{\text{nail}} = 240\) N | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The rigid-jointed plane frame QRS shown in the figure is subjected to a load \( P \) at the joint R. Let the axial deformations in the frame be neglected. If the support S undergoes a settlement of \( \Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{\beta EI} \), the vertical reaction at the support S will become zero when \( \beta \) is equal to
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Indeterminate Structures (Displacement Method)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Rigid-jointed frame QRS with fixed supports at Q and S.
    • Member lengths: \(L_{QR} = L_{RS} = L\)
    • Flexural rigidity: \(EI\) for both members.
    • Axial deformations are negligible.
    • Vertical point load \(P\) acts downwards at joint R.
    • Support S undergoes a downward settlement \(\Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{\beta EI}\)
    • Vertical reaction at S (\(V_S\)) becomes zero.
  • Aim: Determine the value of the coefficient \(\beta\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Slope-Deflection Method: Used to relate member end moments to joint displacements and rotations.
  • Kinematic Indeterminacy: Due to negligible axial deformation, the horizontal displacement of R is zero (\(\delta_{Rx} = 0\)), and its vertical displacement matches the settlement of S exactly (\(\delta_{Ry} = \Delta\)).
  • Joint Equilibrium: The sum of moments at a rigid joint must be zero (\(\sum M_R = 0\)). Also, the sum of forces must balance the external load.
  • Sign Convention: Clockwise moments and rotations are positive. Downward translation is considered as a positive relative displacement for calculating fixed-end moments.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the kinematic degrees of freedom at joint R. Since S settles by \(\Delta\) and axial length RS is rigid, R moves down by \(\Delta\).
  2. Write the slope-deflection equations for members QR and RS.
  3. Apply moment equilibrium at joint R to find the unknown joint rotation \(\theta_R\).
  4. Calculate the shear force exerted by member QR on joint R using the member end moments.
  5. Apply vertical equilibrium at joint R. Since \(V_S = 0\), the axial force in RS is zero. Thus, the vertical shear from QR must completely balance the external load \(P\).
  6. Solve for \(\Delta\) in terms of \(P, L, EI\) and extract \(\beta\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Kinematics of Joint R

  • Displacement of Q: \(\theta_Q = 0,\ \delta_Q = 0\)
  • Displacement of S: \(\theta_S = 0,\ \delta_{S,\text{vertical}} = \Delta\) (downwards)
  • Displacement of R: \(\theta_R \neq 0,\ \delta_{R,\text{vertical}} = \Delta\) (downwards)
  • Relative transverse displacement for QR: \(\Delta_{QR} = \Delta\) (R goes down relative to Q)
  • Relative transverse displacement for RS: \(\Delta_{RS} = 0\) (both R and S go down by \(\Delta\), so no bending due to sway in RS)

Step 2: Slope-Deflection Equations

For member QR (fixed at Q, settles by \(\Delta\) at R):

\[M_{QR} = \dfrac{2EI}{L} \left(2\theta_Q + \theta_R - \dfrac{3\Delta}{L} \right) = \dfrac{2EI}{L} \theta_R - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta \]\[M_{RQ} = \dfrac{2EI}{L} \left(2\theta_R + \theta_Q - \dfrac{3\Delta}{L} \right) = \dfrac{4EI}{L} \theta_R - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta \]

For member RS (fixed at S, no relative transverse sway):

\[M_{RS} = \dfrac{2EI}{L} (2\theta_R + \theta_S - 0) = \dfrac{4EI}{L} \theta_R \]

Step 3: Moment Equilibrium at Joint R

\[\sum M_R = 0 \implies M_{RQ} + M_{RS} = 0 \]\[\left( \dfrac{4EI}{L} \theta_R - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta \right) + \dfrac{4EI}{L} \theta_R = 0 \]\[\dfrac{8EI}{L} \theta_R = \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta \implies \theta_R = \dfrac{3\Delta}{4L} \]

Step 4: Shear Force in Member QR

Substitute \(\theta_R\) back into the moments for QR:

\[M_{QR} = \dfrac{2EI}{L} \left(\dfrac{3\Delta}{4L}\right) - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta = \dfrac{1.5EI}{L^2} \Delta - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta = -4.5 \dfrac{EI}{L^2} \Delta \]\[M_{RQ} = \dfrac{4EI}{L} \left(\dfrac{3\Delta}{4L}\right) - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta = \dfrac{3EI}{L^2} \Delta - \dfrac{6EI}{L^2} \Delta = -3 \dfrac{EI}{L^2} \Delta \]

Sum of end moments: \(M_{QR} + M_{RQ} = -7.5\, \dfrac{EI}{L^2} \Delta\) (Counter-clockwise).
To maintain equilibrium, member QR must be subjected to a clockwise shear couple.

\[V_{QR} \times L = 7.5 \dfrac{EI}{L^2} \Delta \implies V_{QR} = 7.5 \dfrac{EI}{L^3} \Delta \]

This shear acts downwards at end R on the member. Therefore, the member pulls upwards on joint R with a force of \(7.5\, \dfrac{EI}{L^3} \Delta\).

Step 5: Vertical Equilibrium at Joint R

The vertical forces acting on joint R are:

  1. External load \(P\) (downwards)
  2. Upward shear from member QR: \(7.5\, \dfrac{EI}{L^3} \Delta\)
  3. Upward axial force from RS: Given as \(V_S = 0\)
\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies 7.5 \dfrac{EI}{L^3} \Delta - P = 0 \implies \Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{7.5\, EI} \]

Step 6: Determine \(\beta\)

Comparing with the given equation \(\Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{\beta EI}\), we find \(\beta = 7.5\).

6. Final Answer:

\(\beta = 7.5\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A portal frame shown in figure (not drawn to scale) has a hinge support at joint P and a roller support at joint R. A point load of 50 kN is acting at joint R in the horizontal direction. The flexural rigidity, EI, of each member is 10⁶ kNm². Under the applied load, the horizontal displacement (in mm, round off to 1 decimal place) of joint R would be ________
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Frames

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Portal frame with hinge at P and roller at R.
    • Member PQ (horizontal beam) length \(= 5\) m.
    • Member QR (vertical column) length \(= 10\) m.
    • Horizontal Point Load at R \(= 50\) kN.
    • Flexural Rigidity \((EI) = 10^6\text{ kNm}^2\).
  • Aim: Find the horizontal displacement at joint R in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Castigliano's Second Theorem: The partial derivative of the total strain energy \((U)\) of a linearly elastic structure with respect to an applied load \((P)\) is equal to the displacement \((\Delta)\) in the direction of that load.

\[\Delta_R = \dfrac{\partial U}{\partial P} = \int \dfrac{M}{EI} \dfrac{\partial M}{\partial P}\, ds \]

where \(M\) is the internal bending moment written as a function of the generic variable load \(P\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Apply a variable horizontal load \(F\) at the roller support R (where actual load is 50 kN).
  2. Compute the support reactions at P and R in terms of \(F\).
  3. Establish local coordinate systems for members QR and PQ and express the bending moment \(M(x)\) and \(M(y)\) in terms of \(F\).
  4. Find \(\dfrac{\partial M}{\partial F}\) for both members.
  5. Integrate over the lengths of both members to find the displacement.
  6. Substitute the actual load \(F = 50\text{ kN}\) into the final expression.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Reactions under load \(F\) at R

  • P is at \((0, 10)\), Q is at \((5, 10)\), R is at \((5, 0)\). Load \(F\) acts horizontally at R.
  • \(\sum M_P = 0 \Rightarrow V_R \times 5 - F \times 10 = 0 \Rightarrow V_R = 2F\) (Upwards)
  • \(\sum F_y = 0 \Rightarrow V_P = -2F\) (Downwards)
  • \(\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow H_P = -F\) (Leftwards)

Step 2: Bending Moment Equations

  • Member QR: Origin at R, variable \(y\) pointing upwards (\(0 \le y \le 10\)):
    \(M_{QR}(y) = F \cdot y\)    and    \(\dfrac{\partial M_{QR}}{\partial F} = y\)
  • Member PQ: Origin at P, variable \(x\) pointing rightwards (\(0 \le x \le 5\)):
    \(M_{PQ}(x) = V_P \cdot x = 2Fx\)    and    \(\dfrac{\partial M_{PQ}}{\partial F} = 2x\)

Step 3: Apply Castigliano's Theorem

\[\Delta_R = \int_0^{10} \dfrac{(Fy)(y)}{EI}\, dy + \int_0^{5} \dfrac{(2Fx)(2x)}{EI}\, dx \]\[ \Delta_R = \dfrac{F}{EI} \left[\int_0^{10} y^2\, dy + \int_0^{5} 4x^2\, dx \right] \]\[ \Delta_R = \dfrac{F}{EI} \left[\left( \dfrac{y^3}{3} \right)_0^{10} + \left( \dfrac{4x^3}{3} \right)_0^{5} \right] \]\[ \Delta_R = \dfrac{50}{10^6} \left[\dfrac{1000}{3} + \dfrac{4 \times 125}{3} \right] = \dfrac{50}{10^6} \left[\dfrac{1000 + 500}{3} \right] = \dfrac{50}{10^6} \times 500 = \dfrac{25000}{10^6}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Unit Conversion to mm

\[\Delta_R = 0.025\text{ m} \times 1000\text{ mm/m} = 25.0\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Horizontal displacement at R \(= 25.0\) mm | Accepted key range: 24.9 to 25.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A closed thin-walled tube has thickness, \(t\), mean enclosed area within the boundary of the centerline of tube's thickness, \(A_m\), and shear stress, \(\tau\). Torsional moment of resistance, \(T\), of the section would be
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Torsion in Thin-Walled Sections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Tube thickness \(= t\)
    • Mean enclosed area \(= A_m\)
    • Shear stress \(= \tau\)
  • Aim: Determine the Torsional moment of resistance, \(T\).

3. Core Concepts:

Bredt-Batho Theory: Used for analyzing torsion in closed, thin-walled sections (e.g., box girders, tubular shafts).

Shear Flow (\(q\)): The shear force per unit length along the perimeter of the cross-section. It is constant along the perimeter for closed, single-cell thin-walled tubes.

\[q = \tau \times t \]

Torsional Moment (\(T\)): The torque is related to the shear flow and the area enclosed by the median line of the wall thickness.

\[T = 2 \cdot A_m \cdot q \]

4. Solution Method:

The problem is a direct application of the Bredt-Batho formula. By expressing shear flow \(q\) in terms of shear stress \(\tau\) and thickness \(t\), we can immediately find the resisting torque.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Establish the relationship between shear stress and shear flow.\[q = \tau \cdot t \]
  2. Step 2: Express the torsional moment using Bredt's first formula.\[T = 2 \cdot A_m \cdot q \]
  3. Step 3: Substitute \(q\) into the torque equation.\[T = 2 \cdot A_m \cdot (\tau \cdot t) = 2\tau A_m t \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(2\tau A_m t\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: For a channel section subjected to a downward vertical shear force at its centroid, which one of the following represents the correct distribution of shear stress in flange and web?
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Shear Stress Distribution in Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: A channel section subjected to a downward vertical shear force at its centroid.
  • Aim: Identify the correct distribution (direction and shape) of shear stress in the flange and web from the given diagrams.

3. Core Concepts:

Shear Flow (\(q\)): Governed by Jouravski's equation:

\[q = \dfrac{VQ}{I} \]
  • \(V\) = vertical shear force
  • \(Q\) = first moment of area
  • \(I\) = moment of inertia

Continuous Fluid Analogy: In thin-walled open sections, shear flow acts like water flowing continuously through a pipe system. It cannot start or stop abruptly except at free edges (where \(Q = 0\), so \(q = 0\)).

Directionality: The vertical sum of the shear flow in the web must equilibrate the external downward shear force \(V\). Thus, the web shear flow must point downwards.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the shear flow in the web. Since \(V\) is downward, the web shear must point downward.
  2. Apply the continuous flow principle to the flanges. For the flow to be continuous and end up moving downward through the web, it must enter from the top free edge, flow towards the web, go down the web, and then flow outward into the bottom flange towards the bottom free edge.
  3. Examine the shape: \(Q\) varies linearly in the flanges (yielding a linear stress diagram starting from zero at the free edge) and parabolically in the web (yielding a parabolic stress curve maximum at the neutral axis).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Look at the geometry. The web is on the left, and the flanges point to the right. The free edges are on the extreme right of the top and bottom flanges.
  2. Step 2: Apply downward force \(V\). The web arrow must point down.
  3. Step 3: Trace the continuous shear flow path.
    • Top Flange: Starts at zero at the free edge (right). To feed into the top of the web, the flow must move from Right to Left (arrow points Left).
    • Web: Flows from top to bottom (arrow points Down).
    • Bottom Flange: Exits the bottom of the web and moves toward the free edge. Flows from Left to Right (arrow points Right).
  4. Step 4: Check the provided options based on this path (Leftward → Downward → Rightward).
    • (A) Top points Left, Web points Down, Bottom points Right. ✓ Matches perfectly.
    • (B) Top points Left, Bottom points Left. ✗ Violates continuity.
    • (C) Top points Right, Bottom points Right. ✗ Violates continuity.
    • (D) Top points Right, Bottom points Left. ✗ Flow is completely backwards, fighting the downward \(V\).

Note: Because the downward force is applied at the centroid rather than the shear center (which is located to the left of the web), this section will actually twist. However, the question asks for the distribution of shear stress reacting to the primary vertical shear force, which firmly follows profile A.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Matches diagram (A) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The degree of static indeterminacy of the plane frame as shown in the figure is ______
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Kinematic and Static Indeterminacy

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • A 2D plane frame diagram with 3 stories and 2 bays.
    • Supports: Leftmost is Fixed, Middle is Hinged, Rightmost is Hinged.
    • Internal Condition: One internal hinge is present on the middle-left beam.
  • Aim: Determine the degree of static indeterminacy (\(D_s\)) of the given plane frame.

3. Core Concepts:

The degree of static indeterminacy (\(D_s\)) for a 2D rigid plane frame can be calculated using two equivalent methods:

Method A (Formula Based):

\[D_s = (3m + R) - 3j - r_r \]
  • \(m\) = Total number of members
  • \(R\) = Total number of external support reactions
  • \(j\) = Total number of joints (including support joints)
  • \(r_r\) = Total number of released reactions due to internal hinges (\(r_r = m' - 1\), where \(m'\) is the number of members meeting at the internal hinge)

Method B (Closed Loops Method):

\[D_s = 3c - r_s - r_r \]
  • \(c\) = Number of closed loops (or boxes)
  • \(r_s\) = Reactions required to make all supports fully fixed
  • \(r_r\) = Released reactions from internal hinges

4. Solution Method:

Sanity Check of Visuals: Observing standard structural symbols, the leftmost support has a horizontal line with diagonal hatching (Fixed, \(R=3\)). The middle and rightmost supports are triangles with diagonal hatching (Hinged, \(R=2\) each).

5. Step-by-Step Execution (Using Method B — Closed Loops):

  1. Count Closed Loops (\(c\)):
    The frame has 2 bays and 3 stories.\[c = 2 \times 3 = 6 \text{ loops} \]
  2. Calculate Support Releases (\(r_s\)):
    • Left support is fixed → missing 0 reactions.
    • Middle support is hinged → missing 1 moment reaction.
    • Right support is hinged → missing 1 moment reaction.
    \[r_s = 0 + 1 + 1 = 2 \]
  3. Calculate Internal Releases (\(r_r\)):
    An internal hinge is present in the middle of a beam (connecting 2 members).\[r_r = m' - 1 = 2 - 1 = 1 \]
  4. Calculate \(D_s\):\[D_s = 3(6) - 2 - 1 = 18 - 3 = 15 \]

Self-Verification using Method A:

  • Members \(m = 9\) (columns) \(+ 6\) (beams) \(= 15\)
  • Joints \(j = 4\) levels \(\times\, 3\) columns \(= 12\)
  • Reactions \(R = 3\) (Fixed) \(+ 2\) (Hinged) \(+ 2\) (Hinged) \(= 7\)
  • \(D_s = (3 \times 15 + 7) - (3 \times 12) - 1 = 52 - 36 - 1 = 15\)

Both methods yield the exact same result.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 | Accepted key range: 15 to 15

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
For a plane stress problem, the state of stress at a point P is represented by the stress element as shown in figure.


By how much angle (θ) in degrees the stress element should be rotated in order to get the planes of maximum shear stress?
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses and Strains (Mohr's Circle)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: From the provided 2D stress element figure:
    • Normal stress in horizontal direction: \(80\) MPa (Arrows point away → Tension)
    • Normal stress in vertical direction: \(20\) MPa (Arrows point towards the plane → Compression)
    • Shear stress: \(25\) MPa (Right face arrow points upward → Positive per standard sign convention)
  • Aim: Calculate the magnitude of rotation angle (\(\theta\)) in degrees required to reach the planes of maximum shear stress.

3. Core Concepts:

Standard Sign Convention: Tensile normal stresses are positive (\(+\)). Compressive normal stresses are negative (\(-\)). Shear stress that rotates the element counter-clockwise on the right face is positive (\(+\)).

Principal Planes (\(\theta_p\)): The planes of zero shear stress.

\[\tan(2\theta_p) = \dfrac{2\tau_{xy}}{\sigma_x - \sigma_y} \]

Planes of Maximum Shear Stress (\(\theta_s\)): These planes are always offset exactly \(45°\) from the principal planes.

\[\tan(2\theta_s) = -\dfrac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2\tau_{xy}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Carefully extract the stress values with their proper algebraic signs.
  2. Apply the analytical formula for the angle of the maximum shear plane.
  3. Solve for \(2\theta_s\) using the inverse tangent, then halve it to find \(\theta_s\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Assign values with sign conventions.
    \(\sigma_x = +80\) MPa
    \(\sigma_y = -20\) MPa (Crucial Pitfall Avoidance: Visual inspection shows the \(20\) MPa arrows pointing inward against the faces, denoting compression!)
    \(\tau_{xy} = +25\) MPa
  2. Step 2: Plug into the max shear plane formula.\[\tan(2\theta_s) = -\dfrac{80 - (-20)}{2(25)} = -\dfrac{80 + 20}{50} = -\dfrac{100}{50} = -2.0 \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for the angle.\[2\theta_s = \tan^{-1}(-2.0) = -63.43° \]\[\theta_s = -31.71° \]
  4. Step 4: Interpretation.
    The negative sign indicates a clockwise rotation. The magnitude of the required rotation angle to reach the plane of maximum shear stress is \(31.7°\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(31.7°\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A long uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m and a concentrated load of 60 kN are moving together on the beam ABCD shown in the figure (not drawn to scale). The relative positions of the two loads are not fixed. The maximum shear force (in kN, round off to the nearest integer) caused at the internal hinge B due to the two loads is ______
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Influence Line Diagrams (ILD)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Point Load \(P = 60\) kN
    • Uniformly Distributed Load \(w = 10\) kN/m (long, can cover full span)
    • Beam: Hinge support at A, Internal Hinge at B, Rollers at C & D
    • Spans: \(AB = 2\) m, \(BC = 2\) m, \(CD = 4\) m
  • Aim: Find the maximum shear force (reaction transmitted) at the internal hinge B due to these moving loads.

3. Core Concepts:

Statical Determinacy & Load Transfer:

  • The segment \(BCD\) is fully supported by rollers at C and D — it behaves as an independent overhanging beam.
  • The segment \(AB\) is supported by the pin at A and rests on the internal hinge at B (transmitting force to \(BCD\)).
  • Critical realization: Loads placed on \(BCD\) go directly to supports C & D and do not cause any reaction at A or B. Thus, only loads on segment \(AB\) generate a shear force at B.

Influence Line Diagram (ILD) for \(V_B\):

  • If a unit load (\(1\) kN) is at distance \(x\) from A on \(AB\), taking moments about A: \(V_B \times 2 - 1 \times x = 0 \implies V_B = x/2\).
  • Peak ordinate is at B (\(x = 2\)), where \(V_B = 1\).
  • For loads moving on \(BCD\), \(V_B = 0\).
  • The ILD is a triangle spanning A to B with base \(2\) m and maximum height \(1\).

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate parameters of the ILD
    • Maximum Ordinate \((y_{\text{max}}) = 1\) (located at Hinge B)
    • Area under ILD \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 1 = 1\) m
  2. Step 2: Position the loads for maximum effect
    • Point Load (\(P = 60\) kN): Placed exactly over Hinge B (maximum ILD ordinate).\[\text{Force} = 60 \times 1 = 60 \text{ kN} \]
    • UDL (\(w = 10\) kN/m): Spread over the entire positive ILD area (full 2 m length of \(AB\)).\[\text{Force} = 10 \times 1 = 10 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Step 3: Superimpose to get the Maximum Shear Force at B\[\text{Max } V_B = 60 + 10 = 70 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 70 kN | Accepted key range: 70 to 70

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A plane frame shown in the figure (not to scale) has linear elastic springs at node H. The spring constants are kₓ = k = 5 × 10⁵ kN/m and kθ = 3 × 10⁵ kNm/rad.


For the externally applied moment of 30 kNm at node F, the rotation (in degrees, round off to 3 decimals) observed in the rotational spring at node H is ______
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Frames

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Frame geometry: \(L_{EF} = 6\) m, \(L_{FG} = 3\) m, \(L_{GH} = 3\) m
    • Translational spring constants: \(k_x = k_y = 5 \times 10^5\) kN/m
    • Rotational spring constant: \(k_\theta = 3 \times 10^5\) kNm/rad
    • Applied moment: \(M_F = 30\) kNm (counter-clockwise) at node F
    • Support E is a roller support on a horizontal plane.
    • G is an internal hinge.
  • Aim: Determine the rotation at node H in degrees (magnitude).

3. Core Concepts:

Static Equilibrium & Free Body Diagrams (FBD): Split the frame at the internal hinge to isolate forces.

Supports & Hinges: A standard roller support on a horizontal plane provides only a vertical reaction (\(R_x = 0,\ M = 0\)). An internal hinge transfers axial and shear forces but its bending moment is zero.

Spring Rotation: The node H is supported by a rotational spring. The magnitude of its rotation \(\theta_H\) is given by:

\[\theta_H = \dfrac{M_{\text{spring}}}{k_\theta} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Split the frame at the internal hinge G into two sections: E-F-G and G-H.
  2. Consider the left section E-F-G to solve for the vertical reaction at E by taking moments about the hinge G.
  3. Compute the vertical shear force transfer at G.
  4. Consider the right section G-H, loaded with the shear force from G, to find the moment transmitted to node H.
  5. Apply the stiffness formula to find the rotation in radians, and convert to degrees.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Free Body E-F-G:
    The roller at E provides only an upward vertical reaction \(V_E\). Take moments about hinge G:\[\sum M_G = 0 \implies -(V_E \times 3\text{ m}) + 30\text{ kNm} = 0 \implies V_E = 10\text{ kN (upwards)} \]
  2. Vertical force at G on left part using \(\sum F_y = 0\):\[10 + V_{G,\text{left}} = 0 \implies V_{G,\text{left}} = -10\text{ kN} \]By Newton's third law, the right segment (G-H) experiences an upward force \(V_{G,\text{right}} = 10\text{ kN}\).
  3. Free Body G-H:
    Take moments about node H to find \(M_H\):\[\sum M_H = 0 \implies (10\text{ kN} \times 3\text{ m}) - M_H = 0 \implies M_H = 30\text{ kNm (Counter-Clockwise)} \]
  4. Calculate Rotation:\[\theta = \dfrac{M_H}{k_\theta} = \dfrac{30\text{ kNm}}{3 \times 10^5\text{ kNm/rad}} = 10^{-4}\text{ rad} \]
  5. Unit Conversion:\[\theta_{\text{degrees}} = 10^{-4} \times \dfrac{180}{\pi} = 0.00573° \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.006 | Accepted key range: 0.005 to 0.007

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q4
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A column of height \( h \) with a rectangular cross-section of size \( a \times 2a \) has a buckling load of \( P \). If the cross-section is changed to \( 0.5a \times 3a \) and its height changed to \( 1.5h \), the buckling load of the redesigned column will be
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis (Stability) | Euler Buckling of Columns

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Proportionality analysis)
  • Given Data:
    • Original: Cross-section \(a \times 2a\), Height \(h\), Buckling load \(P\)
    • Redesigned: Cross-section \(0.5a \times 3a\), Height \(1.5h\)
  • Aim: Find new buckling load in terms of \(P\).

3. Core Concepts:

Euler Buckling Load:

\[P_{cr} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E I_{min}}{L_{eff}^2} \implies P_{cr} \propto \dfrac{I_{min}}{h^2} \]

Moment of Inertia for Rectangle:

  • About major axis: \(I_{xx} = \dfrac{bd^3}{12}\)
  • About minor axis: \(I_{yy} = \dfrac{db^3}{12}\)

For buckling, \(I_{min}\) governs (column buckles about the weaker axis).

4. Solution Method:

Calculate \(I_{min}\) for both configurations and apply proportionality.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Original Column (\(b_1 = a,\ d_1 = 2a,\ h_1 = h\)):

ParameterValue
\(I_{xx,1}\)\(\dfrac{a(2a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{2a^4}{3}\)
\(I_{yy,1}\) (Minimum ✓)\(\dfrac{2a \cdot a^3}{12} = \dfrac{a^4}{6}\)
\[P = \dfrac{\pi^2 E \cdot \dfrac{a^4}{6}}{h^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{6h^2} \]

Redesigned Column (\(b_2 = 0.5a,\ d_2 = 3a,\ h_2 = 1.5h\)):

ParameterValue
\(I_{xx,2}\)\(\dfrac{0.5a \cdot (3a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{9a^4}{8}\)
\(I_{yy,2}\) (Minimum ✓)\(\dfrac{3a \cdot (0.5a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{a^4}{32}\)
